`no_shared_cds` rows show counts only (no percentage).

Note: the coding pair count here differs from Table 2 because `compareIsoformFrames()`
classifies some individually-coding pairs as `no_shared_cds` (both isoforms are
coding but their CDS regions don't overlap). Table 2's "coding pairs" filter
requires only that both isoforms have `coding_status == "coding"` in `cds.rds`.

## How PTCs Arise: Frameshift vs Non-Frameshift Mechanisms

```{r goal2-ptc-mechanisms}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: computed inline in this report (not a separate script)
# Methods: METHODS.md § "PTC-Causing Event Attribution"
#
# For each PTC+ NMD comparator, identify the PTC-CAUSING splice event:
#   - Frameshift PTCs: from analyzeFrameWalk() (Isopair::analyzeFrameWalk,
#     cached as fw_c2_allsamples.rds by 03_nmd_analysis_mashr.Rmd)
#   - Non-frameshift PTCs: the event whose genomic coordinates (from
#     buildProfiles() detailed_events) contain the strand-aware PTC position
#     (from Isopair::extractCds → cds.rds)
#
# Strand-aware PTC position:
#   + strand: PTC = cds_stop (larger genomic coordinate = 3' end of CDS)
#   - strand: PTC = cds_start (smaller genomic coordinate = 3' end on minus strand)
# For PTC isoforms, SQANTI annotates the actual (premature) stop, so cds_start/
# cds_stop IS the PTC position (depending on strand).

fc_c2 <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$frame_comp
fw_c2 <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$frame_walk
prof_c2 <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$profiles

fc_c2_ps <- fc_c2$pair_summary
fc_c2_ps$has_ptc <- fc_c2_ps$comparator_isoform_id %in% ptc_pos_ids

frameshift_cats <- c("same_start_frameshift",
                     "diff_start_diff_frame_with_frameshift")
fc_c2_ps$is_frameshift_cat <- fc_c2_ps$frame_category %in% frameshift_cats

# PTC+ pairs by mechanism — restrict to coding pairs (both ref and comp coding)
# to match the coding_pairs_c2 base used in Goals 3-4 and the cumulative flowchart
coding_ids_g2 <- cds$isoform_id[cds$coding_status == "coding"]
ptc_plus <- fc_c2_ps[fc_c2_ps$has_ptc == TRUE &
  fc_c2_ps$comparator_isoform_id %in% coding_ids_g2 &
  fc_c2_ps$reference_isoform_id %in% coding_ids_g2, ]
n_ptc_via_fs    <- sum(ptc_plus$is_frameshift_cat)
n_ptc_via_nonfs <- sum(!ptc_plus$is_frameshift_cat)
n_ptc_total     <- nrow(ptc_plus)

# Also count all coding NMD pairs for context (same coding filter as ptc_plus)
fc_c2_coding <- fc_c2_ps[fc_c2_ps$comparator_isoform_id %in% coding_ids_g2 &
  fc_c2_ps$reference_isoform_id %in% coding_ids_g2, ]
n_coding_nmd <- nrow(fc_c2_coding)

# ── Strand-aware PTC position lookups ──
# On + strand the stop codon is at cds_stop (larger coordinate).
# On - strand the stop codon is at cds_start (smaller coordinate).
cds_start_lookup <- setNames(cds$cds_start, cds$isoform_id)
cds_stop_lookup  <- setNames(cds$cds_stop, cds$isoform_id)
strand_lookup    <- setNames(cds$strand, cds$isoform_id)

# Build lookup: comparator_id → row index in prof_c2
comp_to_idx <- setNames(seq_len(nrow(prof_c2)), prof_c2$comparator_isoform_id)

# Frameshift PTC-causing events (from frame_walk)
fw_fs <- fw_c2$events[fw_c2$events$is_frameshift == TRUE, ]

ptc_event_rows <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(ptc_plus))) {
  comp_id <- ptc_plus$comparator_isoform_id[i]
  is_fs <- ptc_plus$is_frameshift_cat[i]

  if (is_fs) {
    # Frameshift PTC: use the frameshift-causing event from frame_walk
    fs_match <- fw_fs[fw_fs$comparator_isoform_id == comp_id, ]
    if (nrow(fs_match) > 0) {
      ptc_event_rows[[length(ptc_event_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        comparator_id = comp_id,
        mechanism = "Frameshift",
        ptc_causing_event = fs_match$event_type[1],
        attribution = "direct",
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    } else {
      # Frameshift category but no is_frameshift event in frame_walk.
      # This indicates a disagreement between compareIsoformFrames() and
      # analyzeFrameWalk() — do not guess; label as unresolved.
      ptc_event_rows[[length(ptc_event_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        comparator_id = comp_id,
        mechanism = "Frameshift",
        ptc_causing_event = "Unresolved",
        attribution = "unresolved",
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }
  } else {
    # Non-frameshift PTC: find the event containing the strand-aware PTC position
    prof_idx <- comp_to_idx[comp_id]
    if (is.na(prof_idx)) next
    de <- prof_c2$detailed_events[[prof_idx]]
    if (is.null(de) || nrow(de) == 0) next

    # Strand-aware PTC genomic position
    comp_strand <- strand_lookup[comp_id]
    ptc_pos_genomic <- if (!is.na(comp_strand) && comp_strand == "-") {
      cds_start_lookup[comp_id]
    } else {
      cds_stop_lookup[comp_id]
    }
    if (is.na(ptc_pos_genomic)) next

    # Check which event's coordinates span the PTC position
    de$ev_min <- pmin(de$five_prime, de$three_prime)
    de$ev_max <- pmax(de$five_prime, de$three_prime)
    containing <- de[ptc_pos_genomic >= de$ev_min & ptc_pos_genomic <= de$ev_max, ]

    if (nrow(containing) > 0) {
      ptc_event_rows[[length(ptc_event_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        comparator_id = comp_id,
        mechanism = "In-frame stop",
        ptc_causing_event = containing$event_type[1],
        attribution = "direct",
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    } else {
      ptc_event_rows[[length(ptc_event_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        comparator_id = comp_id,
        mechanism = "In-frame stop",
        ptc_causing_event = "Unresolved",
        attribution = "unresolved",
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }
  }
}

ptc_events_df <- do.call(rbind, ptc_event_rows)
n_attributed <- sum(ptc_events_df$attribution == "direct")
n_unresolved <- sum(ptc_events_df$attribution == "unresolved")
```

Of `r fmt(n_coding_nmd)` coding NMD pairs, `r fmt(n_ptc_total)` have a PTC in
the comparator. These arise through two mechanisms:

- **Frameshift → PTC**: `r fmt(n_ptc_via_fs)` pairs
  (`r round(100 * n_ptc_via_fs / n_ptc_total, 1)`%) — a splicing event shifts
  the reading frame, and the new frame encounters a premature stop codon. The
  PTC-causing event is identified by `analyzeFrameWalk()`.
- **In-frame stop → PTC**: `r fmt(n_ptc_via_nonfs)` pairs
  (`r round(100 * n_ptc_via_nonfs / n_ptc_total, 1)`%) — the comparator is
  in the same reading frame but a structural change (e.g., a gained exon or
  retained intron) directly introduces an in-frame stop codon. The PTC-causing
  event is identified by finding the event whose genomic coordinates contain the
  comparator's stop codon position.

### PTC position and strand awareness

The PTC genomic position depends on strand: for + strand genes, the stop codon
is at `cds_stop` (the larger genomic coordinate); for - strand genes, it is at
`cds_start` (the smaller genomic coordinate, which is the 3' end in
transcription direction). This mirrors the logic in `Isopair::computePtcStatus`.

### Attribution results

Of `r fmt(nrow(ptc_events_df))` PTC+ pairs, `r fmt(n_attributed)` were
directly attributed (PTC position inside event coordinates or frameshift event
from `analyzeFrameWalk`)`r if (n_unresolved > 0) paste0(", and ", fmt(n_unresolved), " remain unresolved")``r if (n_unresolved == 0) ""`.
`r if (n_unresolved > 0) "Unresolved cases include both in-frame stop pairs where the PTC falls outside all event coordinates and frameshift-category pairs where analyzeFrameWalk() found no frameshift event (indicating a classification disagreement between compareIsoformFrames() and analyzeFrameWalk())."`

```{r goal2-ptc-diagnostic, eval = n_unresolved > 0}
# ── Diagnostic: characterize all unresolved PTC attributions ──
# Two types of unresolved:
#   1. In-frame stop: PTC position outside all event coordinates
#   2. Frameshift: frame_category says frameshift but analyzeFrameWalk() found
#      no is_frameshift event (classification disagreement)
# For each, report mechanism, strand, frame_category, and distance to nearest event.

unresolved <- ptc_events_df[ptc_events_df$attribution == "unresolved", ]

diag_rows <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(unresolved))) {
  uid <- unresolved$comparator_id[i]
  mech <- unresolved$mechanism[i]

  prof_idx <- comp_to_idx[uid]
  fc_row <- fc_c2_ps[fc_c2_ps$comparator_isoform_id == uid, ]
  gene_id <- if (nrow(fc_row) > 0) fc_row$gene_id[1] else NA_character_
  frame_cat <- if (nrow(fc_row) > 0) fc_row$frame_category[1] else NA_character_
  comp_strand <- strand_lookup[uid]

  # PTC position and distance to nearest event (if events exist)
  ptc_pos <- if (!is.na(comp_strand) && comp_strand == "-") {
    cds_start_lookup[uid]
  } else {
    cds_stop_lookup[uid]
  }

  nearest_evt <- NA_character_; min_dist <- NA_real_; n_ev <- 0L
  if (!is.na(prof_idx)) {
    de <- prof_c2$detailed_events[[prof_idx]]
    if (!is.null(de) && nrow(de) > 0) {
      n_ev <- nrow(de)
      if (!is.na(ptc_pos)) {
        de$ev_min <- pmin(de$five_prime, de$three_prime)
        de$ev_max <- pmax(de$five_prime, de$three_prime)
        nearest_idx <- which.min(pmin(abs(ptc_pos - de$ev_min),
                                      abs(ptc_pos - de$ev_max)))
        min_dist <- min(abs(ptc_pos - c(de$ev_min, de$ev_max)))
        nearest_evt <- de$event_type[nearest_idx]
      }
    }
  }

  diag_rows[[length(diag_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
    comparator_id = uid, gene_id = gene_id, mechanism = mech,
    strand = comp_strand, frame_category = frame_cat,
    ptc_pos = if (is.na(ptc_pos)) NA_real_ else ptc_pos,
    nearest_event_type = nearest_evt,
    dist_to_nearest_boundary = min_dist,
    n_events = n_ev,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
diag_df <- do.call(rbind, diag_rows)
diag_df <- diag_df[order(diag_df$mechanism, diag_df$dist_to_nearest_boundary), ]

render_dt(diag_df,
  caption = paste0("Diagnostic: ", nrow(diag_df),
    " Unresolved PTC Attributions"))
```

`r if (n_unresolved > 0) paste0("The diagnostic table shows ", fmt(n_unresolved), " unresolved cases. **Mechanism** distinguishes the two types: *In-frame stop* pairs have a PTC outside all event coordinates (dist_to_nearest_boundary shows how far); *Frameshift* pairs have a frameshift frame_category but analyzeFrameWalk() found no is_frameshift event, indicating a classification disagreement between the two Isopair functions.")`

```{r goal2-ptc-fs-test}
# ── Data provenance ──
# n_ptc_via_fs, n_ptc_total: from goal2-ptc-mechanisms chunk
# Baseline: frameshift rate among ALL coding NMD pairs (not just PTC+)
# fc_c2_ps$is_frameshift_cat: TRUE for frameshift frame categories
# Binomial test: is the frameshift proportion among PTC+ pairs different
#   from the frameshift proportion among all coding NMD pairs?

n_fs_all_nmd <- sum(fc_c2_coding$is_frameshift_cat)
baseline_fs_rate <- n_fs_all_nmd / n_coding_nmd

bt_fs <- binom.test(n_ptc_via_fs, n_ptc_total, p = baseline_fs_rate)
```

Frameshifts account for **`r fmt(n_ptc_via_fs)`** of **`r fmt(n_ptc_total)`**
PTC events in NMD pairs (**`r round(100 * n_ptc_via_fs / n_ptc_total, 1)`%**),
with in-frame stops accounting for the remaining
**`r round(100 * n_ptc_via_nonfs / n_ptc_total, 1)`%** — the two mechanisms
contribute roughly equally. However, frameshifts are significantly enriched
among PTC+ pairs relative to the overall frameshift rate among all coding NMD
pairs (`r round(100 * baseline_fs_rate, 1)`%; binomial test p =
`r signif(bt_fs$p.value, 3)`).

## Figure 6: PTC-Causing Splice Events (Sankey)

```{r goal2-fig5-sankey}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Combines three sources of PTC attribution:
#   1. Diff-stop frameshift: ptc_events_df (from analyzeFrameWalk)
#   2. Diff-stop in-frame: ptc_events_df (from coordinate containment)
#   3. Same-stop (3'UTR splice): attributed here using nearest-to-stop 3'UTR event
# Same-stop attribution: for each same-stop pair, find splice events downstream
# of the stop codon and attribute to the nearest one (the junction most likely
# to place the critical EJC within the >50 nt window).

# ── Identify same-stop PTC+ pairs (strand-aware) ──
# This duplicates the strand-aware stop comparison from goal3-fig6-pop,
# which has not yet run. Uses the same logic: + strand → cds_stop, - strand → cds_start.
ptc_plus_sankey <- ptc_plus  # from goal2-ptc-mechanisms
ptc_plus_sankey$strand_s <- strand_lookup[ptc_plus_sankey$comparator_isoform_id]
ptc_plus_sankey$comp_stop_s <- ifelse(ptc_plus_sankey$strand_s == "-",
  cds_start_lookup[ptc_plus_sankey$comparator_isoform_id],
  cds_stop_lookup[ptc_plus_sankey$comparator_isoform_id])
ptc_plus_sankey$ref_stop_s <- ifelse(ptc_plus_sankey$strand_s == "-",
  cds_start_lookup[ptc_plus_sankey$reference_isoform_id],
  cds_stop_lookup[ptc_plus_sankey$reference_isoform_id])
ptc_plus_sankey$same_stop_s <- ptc_plus_sankey$comp_stop_s == ptc_plus_sankey$ref_stop_s

same_stop_sankey <- ptc_plus_sankey[which(ptc_plus_sankey$same_stop_s == TRUE), ]

# ── Attribute same-stop pairs to nearest 3'UTR event ──
same_stop_attr <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(same_stop_sankey))) {
  comp_id <- same_stop_sankey$comparator_isoform_id[i]
  stop_pos <- same_stop_sankey$comp_stop_s[i]
  comp_strand <- same_stop_sankey$strand_s[i]

  prof_idx <- comp_to_idx[comp_id]
  if (is.na(prof_idx)) next
  de <- prof_c2$detailed_events[[prof_idx]]
  if (is.null(de) || nrow(de) == 0) next

  # Find events downstream of stop in transcription direction
  if (comp_strand == "+") {
    utr3_ev <- de[de$five_prime >= stop_pos | de$three_prime >= stop_pos, ]
    if (nrow(utr3_ev) == 0) next
    ev_starts <- pmin(utr3_ev$five_prime, utr3_ev$three_prime)
    nearest_idx <- which.min(ev_starts - stop_pos)
  } else {
    utr3_ev <- de[de$five_prime <= stop_pos | de$three_prime <= stop_pos, ]
    if (nrow(utr3_ev) == 0) next
    ev_ends <- pmax(utr3_ev$five_prime, utr3_ev$three_prime)
    nearest_idx <- which.min(stop_pos - ev_ends)
  }

  same_stop_attr[[length(same_stop_attr) + 1]] <- data.frame(
    comparator_id = comp_id,
    mechanism = "3'UTR splice",
    ptc_causing_event = utr3_ev$event_type[nearest_idx],
    attribution = "direct",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
same_stop_events <- do.call(rbind, same_stop_attr)
n_same_stop_attributed <- nrow(same_stop_events)

# ── Combine all attributed pairs ──
# Diff-stop attributed (from goal2-ptc-mechanisms), excluding same-stop pairs.
# Same-stop pairs may have been "directly" attributed in goal2 if the stop
# position fell inside an event by coincidence — these belong in 3'UTR splice.
# Pairs with unknown ref stop (coding_status="unknown") are kept in diff-stop.
same_stop_comp_ids <- same_stop_sankey$comparator_isoform_id
diffstop_attr <- ptc_events_df[ptc_events_df$attribution == "direct" &
  !ptc_events_df$comparator_id %in% same_stop_comp_ids, ]
# Same-stop attributed (from above)
all_attr <- rbind(diffstop_attr, same_stop_events)

# Shorten event type labels
all_attr$event_short <- all_attr$ptc_causing_event
all_attr$event_short[all_attr$event_short == "Missing_Internal"] <- "Missing Int."
all_attr$event_short[all_attr$event_short == "Partial_IR_5"] <- "Partial IR 5'"
all_attr$event_short[all_attr$event_short == "Partial_IR_3"] <- "Partial IR 3'"
all_attr$event_short[all_attr$event_short == "Alt_TSS"] <- "Alt TSS"
all_attr$event_short[all_attr$event_short == "Alt_TES"] <- "Alt TES"
all_attr$event_short[all_attr$event_short == "IR_diff"] <- "IR diff"
all_attr$event_short[all_attr$event_short == "IR_diff_3"] <- "IR diff 3'"
all_attr$event_short[all_attr$event_short == "IR_diff_5"] <- "IR diff 5'"

# Collapse rare event types (<3 occurrences) into "Other"
evt_counts <- table(all_attr$event_short)
rare_events <- names(evt_counts[evt_counts < 3])
all_attr$event_short[all_attr$event_short %in% rare_events] <- "Other"

# Also make ptc_attr available for Table 5a/5b (diff-stop attributed only)
ptc_attr <- all_attr[all_attr$mechanism != "3'UTR splice", ]

# Aggregate: event_type → mechanism
sankey_agg <- all_attr |>
  group_by(event_short, mechanism) |>
  summarise(freq = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Build networkD3 data structures
nodes_vec <- unique(c(sankey_agg$event_short, sankey_agg$mechanism))
nodes <- data.frame(name = nodes_vec, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

links <- data.frame(
  source = match(sankey_agg$event_short, nodes_vec) - 1L,
  target = match(sankey_agg$mechanism, nodes_vec) - 1L,
  value  = sankey_agg$freq
)

# Node colors: mechanism nodes colored, event types grey
mech_colors <- c("Frameshift" = "#d6604d",
                 "In-frame stop" = "#4393c3",
                 "3'UTR splice" = "#66c2a5")
node_colors <- ifelse(nodes$name %in% names(mech_colors),
                      mech_colors[nodes$name], "#bdbdbd")

color_scale <- paste0(
  'd3.scaleOrdinal().domain([',
  paste0('"', nodes$name, '"', collapse = ','), ']).range([',
  paste0('"', node_colors, '"', collapse = ','), '])')

networkD3::sankeyNetwork(
  Links = links, Nodes = nodes,
  Source = "source", Target = "target", Value = "value",
  NodeID = "name", fontSize = 14, nodeWidth = 30, nodePadding = 15,
  colourScale = color_scale, sinksRight = TRUE)
```

This figure maps each PTC-causing splice event to one of three mechanisms:
**Frameshift** (red; `r fmt(sum(all_attr$mechanism == "Frameshift"))` pairs) —
a splice event shifts the reading frame, introducing a new stop codon;
**In-frame stop** (blue; `r fmt(sum(all_attr$mechanism == "In-frame stop"))`) —
a splice event introduces an in-frame stop codon directly;
**3'UTR splice** (green; `r fmt(n_same_stop_attributed)`) —
the comparator shares the reference's stop codon, but a downstream splice event
repositions an EJC, making the normal stop "premature." For 3'UTR splice pairs,
the attributed event is the nearest downstream event to the stop codon.
`r { n_same_stop_unresolved_in_goal2 <- sum(ptc_events_df$attribution == "unresolved" & ptc_events_df$comparator_id %in% same_stop_comp_ids); n_diffstop_unresolved <- n_unresolved - n_same_stop_unresolved_in_goal2; n_same_no_event <- nrow(same_stop_sankey) - n_same_stop_attributed; paste0(fmt(n_diffstop_unresolved), " unresolved diff-stop pairs and ", fmt(n_same_no_event), " same-stop pairs without identifiable 3'UTR events are excluded (", fmt(nrow(all_attr)), " of ", fmt(nrow(ptc_plus)), " PTC+ pairs shown).") }`

## Table 5a: PTC-Causing Events by Mechanism

```{r goal2-fig5-summary}
# Summary table of PTC-causing events by mechanism
# Denominator: all directly attributed pairs (excludes unresolved)
ptc_event_summary <- ptc_attr |>
  group_by(mechanism, ptc_causing_event) |>
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(mechanism, desc(n))
ptc_event_summary$pct <- round(100 * ptc_event_summary$n / nrow(ptc_attr), 1)

render_dt(ptc_event_summary, caption = "Table 5a: PTC-Causing Events by Mechanism (NMD)")
write.csv(ptc_event_summary, file.path(table_dir, "table5a_ptc_causing_events.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

Columns: **mechanism** = Frameshift or In-frame stop; **ptc_causing_event** =
splice event type that caused the PTC; **n** = number of pairs; **pct** =
percentage of all `r fmt(nrow(ptc_attr))` attributed PTCs.

## Table 5b: PTC-Causing Event Proportions vs Control Baseline

```{r goal2-table4b-baseline}
# ── Data provenance ──
# NMD: PTC-causing events attributed above (both frameshift and in-frame stop)
# Control baseline: all splicing events across all C4 pairs
# Comparison: proportion of each event type among PTC-causing NMD events vs
#   all Control events (the baseline frequency in normal alternative splicing)

# NMD PTC-causing event frequencies (attributed pairs: direct + largest_event)
n_ptc_attr <- nrow(ptc_attr)
ptc_evt_freq <- sort(table(ptc_attr$ptc_causing_event), decreasing = TRUE)
ptc_evt_df <- data.frame(
  event_type = names(ptc_evt_freq),
  n_ptc_events = as.integer(ptc_evt_freq),
  pct_of_ptc = round(100 * as.integer(ptc_evt_freq) / n_ptc_attr, 1),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Control baseline: all events across all C4 pairs
ctrl_all_events <- do.call(rbind, set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$profiles$detailed_events)
ctrl_event_freq <- table(ctrl_all_events$event_type)
ctrl_total <- sum(ctrl_event_freq)

# Merge
ptc_evt_df$n_ctrl_events <- as.integer(ctrl_event_freq[ptc_evt_df$event_type])
ptc_evt_df$n_ctrl_events[is.na(ptc_evt_df$n_ctrl_events)] <- 0L
ptc_evt_df$pct_ctrl <- round(100 * ptc_evt_df$n_ctrl_events / ctrl_total, 1)
ptc_evt_df$enrichment <- round(ptc_evt_df$pct_of_ptc / pmax(ptc_evt_df$pct_ctrl, 0.1), 1)

# Fisher's exact test per event type: is this event over-represented among
# PTC-causing events vs all Control events?
ptc_evt_df$fisher_p <- NA_real_
ptc_evt_df$direction <- NA_character_
for (i in seq_len(nrow(ptc_evt_df))) {
  a <- ptc_evt_df$n_ptc_events[i]      # this event in PTC-causing
  b <- n_ptc_attr - a                    # other events in PTC-causing
  c_val <- ptc_evt_df$n_ctrl_events[i]  # this event in Control
  d_val <- ctrl_total - c_val            # other events in Control
  ft <- tryCatch(fisher.test(matrix(c(a, b, c_val, d_val), nrow = 2)),
                 error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(ft)) {
    ptc_evt_df$fisher_p[i] <- signif(ft$p.value, 3)
    ptc_evt_df$direction[i] <- if (ft$p.value > 0.05) "Non-significant"
      else if (ptc_evt_df$enrichment[i] > 1) "Enriched in PTC-causing"
      else "Depleted in PTC-causing"
  }
}

render_dt(ptc_evt_df, caption = "Table 5b: PTC-Causing Events (NMD) vs All Events (Control)")
write.csv(ptc_evt_df, file.path(table_dir, "table5b_ptc_event_enrichment.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

Columns: **event_type** = splice event type; **n_ptc_events** = count of
PTC-causing events of this type; **pct_of_ptc** = % of all
`r fmt(n_ptc_attr)` attributed PTC-causing events; **n_ctrl_events** = count in
gene-matched Control (C4) pairs; **pct_ctrl** = % of `r fmt(ctrl_total)` Control
events; **enrichment** = fold enrichment (% PTC / % Ctrl); **fisher_p** =
Fisher's exact test p-value (2×2: this event vs others × PTC-causing vs
Control); **direction** = Enriched/Depleted in PTC-causing, or Non-significant
(p > 0.05).


# 4. Non-PTC NMD Triggers {#goal4}

**Goal 4:** Characterize NMD-responsive comparator isoforms that lack a PTC.

**Methods:** Among coding NMD (C2) comparators, a substantial fraction lack a PTC (stop
codon >50 nt upstream of last EJC). We categorize these PTC-negative NMD isoforms by:
(a) borderline PTC position (stop codon with 1+ downstream EJCs but within 50 nt),
(b) 3'UTR exonic length, (c) frame category, and (d) NMD response magnitude.

```{r goal3-identify-ptc-neg}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Starting data: gene-matched C2 all_samples profiles → cached PTC association
# ptc_c2_as = set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$ptc_assoc
#   Source: testPtcAssociation(ptc, gene-matched profiles), cached by script 03
#   $pair_summary: one row per gene-matched pair, with comp_has_ptc flag
# Step 1: Filter to coding pairs (both ref and comp in cds$coding_status == "coding")
# Step 2: Split into PTC+ and PTC- NMD comparators

ptc_c2_as <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$ptc_assoc
pair_summary <- ptc_c2_as$pair_summary

# Restrict to coding pairs (same filter as Table 2)
coding_ids_g3 <- cds$isoform_id[cds$coding_status == "coding"]
coding_pairs_c2 <- pair_summary[pair_summary$comparator_isoform_id %in% coding_ids_g3 &
                                  pair_summary$reference_isoform_id %in% coding_ids_g3, ]

n_ptc_pos <- sum(coding_pairs_c2$comp_has_ptc == TRUE)
n_ptc_neg <- sum(coding_pairs_c2$comp_has_ptc == FALSE)
```

Of the `r fmt(nrow(set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$profiles))` gene-matched NMD
pairs, `r fmt(nrow(coding_pairs_c2))` are coding pairs (both reference and
comparator classified as protein-coding). Among these,
`r fmt(n_ptc_pos)` (`r round(100 * n_ptc_pos / nrow(coding_pairs_c2), 1)`%)
have a PTC (comparator stop codon >50 nt upstream of last EJC) and
`r fmt(n_ptc_neg)` (`r round(100 * n_ptc_neg / nrow(coding_pairs_c2), 1)`%)
do not. The remainder of this section characterizes these
`r fmt(n_ptc_neg)` **PTC-negative NMD comparators**.

## Categorization by Stop Codon Position

```{r goal3-stop-position}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Starting data: ptc_neg_ids (PTC-negative NMD comparators identified above)
# ptc.rds: per-isoform annotations (n_downstream_ejcs, ptc_distance, etc.)
#   Source: Isopair testPtcAssociation() infrastructure — isoform-intrinsic
# Step 1: Look up ptc features for PTC-neg comparators
# Step 2: Categorize by n_downstream_ejcs (borderline vs stop-in-last-exon)

ptc_neg_ids <- coding_pairs_c2$comparator_isoform_id[coding_pairs_c2$comp_has_ptc == FALSE]
ptc_neg_info <- ptc[ptc$isoform_id %in% ptc_neg_ids, ]

# Categorize
n_borderline <- sum(ptc_neg_info$n_downstream_ejcs > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
n_stop_last_exon <- sum(ptc_neg_info$n_downstream_ejcs == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
n_na <- sum(is.na(ptc_neg_info$n_downstream_ejcs))

stop_cat <- data.frame(
  category = c("Borderline (1+ downstream EJCs, distance <= 50 nt)",
               "Stop in last exon (0 downstream EJCs)",
               "Missing annotation"),
  n = c(n_borderline, n_stop_last_exon, n_na),
  pct = round(100 * c(n_borderline, n_stop_last_exon, n_na) / length(ptc_neg_ids), 1))

kable(stop_cat, caption = "Table 6: Categorization of PTC-Negative NMD Comparators")
```

## Figure 7: 3'UTR Length by PTC Mechanism

```{r goal3-fig6-pop}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: computed inline in this report using cached divergence + cds.rds
# Methods: METHODS.md § "3'UTR Length Analysis with PTC Correction"
# Key functions:
#   Isopair::quantifyPairDivergence() → div_c2/div_c4 (utr3_bp_comp column)
#   Isopair::.computeRegionalBp() → computes 3'UTR as exonic bp after cds_stop
#   Reference-based 3'UTR: computed inline using ref cds_stop on comp exon structure
# Starting data: gene-matched C2 and C4 profiles → cached divergence
# PTC mechanism classification: "same stop" vs "diff stop"
#   same_stop: comparator and reference share the same cds_stop position.
#     The PTC arises because a 3'UTR splicing event repositioned the last EJC
#     downstream, making the existing stop codon >50 nt upstream of the new EJC.
#     The 3'UTR length measurement (from cds_stop to tx end) is correct and
#     unaffected by the PTC classification.
#   diff_stop: comparator has a different cds_stop (= premature stop from
#     frameshift or in-frame stop in the CDS). The measured 3'UTR is inflated
#     because it includes the former CDS region between PTC and normal stop.
#     For these, we also compute a "reference-based 3'UTR": exonic bp downstream
#     of the REFERENCE's cds_stop in the COMPARATOR's exon structure. This is
#     only valid when the reference stop position falls within the comparator's
#     exons (86% of cases).

div_c2 <- set_results[["c2_allsamples"]]$divergence
div_c4 <- set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$divergence
ptc_pos_comp_ids <- coding_pairs_c2$comparator_isoform_id[coding_pairs_c2$comp_has_ptc == TRUE]

# Classify PTC+ by same vs different stop codon position
# Strand-aware: + strand stop = cds_stop; - strand stop = cds_start
cds_start_lookup_g3 <- setNames(cds$cds_start, cds$isoform_id)
cds_stop_lookup_g3  <- setNames(cds$cds_stop, cds$isoform_id)
strand_lookup_g3    <- setNames(cds$strand, cds$isoform_id)

ptc_pos_ps <- coding_pairs_c2[coding_pairs_c2$comp_has_ptc == TRUE, ]
ptc_pos_ps$strand <- strand_lookup_g3[ptc_pos_ps$comparator_isoform_id]
ptc_pos_ps$comp_stop <- ifelse(ptc_pos_ps$strand == "-",
  cds_start_lookup_g3[ptc_pos_ps$comparator_isoform_id],
  cds_stop_lookup_g3[ptc_pos_ps$comparator_isoform_id])
ptc_pos_ps$ref_stop <- ifelse(ptc_pos_ps$strand == "-",
  cds_start_lookup_g3[ptc_pos_ps$reference_isoform_id],
  cds_stop_lookup_g3[ptc_pos_ps$reference_isoform_id])
ptc_pos_ps$same_stop <- ptc_pos_ps$comp_stop == ptc_pos_ps$ref_stop

same_stop_ids <- ptc_pos_ps$comparator_isoform_id[ptc_pos_ps$same_stop == TRUE]
diff_stop_ids <- ptc_pos_ps$comparator_isoform_id[ptc_pos_ps$same_stop == FALSE]

# For diff-stop pairs, compute reference-based 3'UTR
diff_stop_ps <- ptc_pos_ps[ptc_pos_ps$same_stop == FALSE, ]
ref_based_utr3 <- setNames(rep(NA_integer_, nrow(diff_stop_ps)), diff_stop_ps$comparator_isoform_id)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(diff_stop_ps))) {
  comp_id <- diff_stop_ps$comparator_isoform_id[i]
  ref_stop_pos <- diff_stop_ps$ref_stop[i]
  comp_strand <- strand_lookup_g3[comp_id]
  if (is.na(comp_strand) || is.na(ref_stop_pos)) next

  str_row <- structures[structures$isoform_id == comp_id, ]
  if (nrow(str_row) == 0) next
  exon_s <- str_row$exon_starts[[1]]
  exon_e <- str_row$exon_ends[[1]]

  # Check ref stop is in comparator exons
  in_exon <- any(ref_stop_pos >= exon_s & ref_stop_pos <= exon_e)
  if (!in_exon) next

  utr3 <- 0L
  for (k in seq_along(exon_s)) {
    if (comp_strand == "+") {
      if (exon_e[k] > ref_stop_pos) {
        post_start <- max(exon_s[k], ref_stop_pos + 1L)
        utr3 <- utr3 + as.integer(exon_e[k] - post_start + 1L)
      }
    } else {
      if (exon_s[k] < ref_stop_pos) {
        pre_end <- min(exon_e[k], ref_stop_pos - 1L)
        utr3 <- utr3 + as.integer(pre_end - exon_s[k] + 1L)
      }
    }
  }
  ref_based_utr3[comp_id] <- utr3
}

n_eligible <- sum(!is.na(ref_based_utr3))
n_ineligible <- sum(is.na(ref_based_utr3))

# Lookup for comparator 3'UTR from divergence
utr3_comp_lk <- setNames(div_c2$utr3_bp_comp, div_c2$comparator_isoform_id)

# Build 5-group data
utr3_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(group = "Same-stop PTC+\n(3'UTR splicing)",
    utr3_bp = utr3_comp_lk[same_stop_ids]),
  data.frame(group = "Diff-stop PTC+\n(own stop, inflated)",
    utr3_bp = utr3_comp_lk[diff_stop_ids]),
  data.frame(group = "Diff-stop PTC+\n(ref stop, corrected)",
    utr3_bp = ref_based_utr3[!is.na(ref_based_utr3)]),
  data.frame(group = "NMD PTC-",
    utr3_bp = utr3_comp_lk[ptc_neg_ids]),
  data.frame(group = "Control",
    utr3_bp = div_c4$utr3_bp_comp)
)
utr3_data <- utr3_data[!is.na(utr3_data$utr3_bp) & utr3_data$utr3_bp > 0, ]
utr3_data$group <- factor(utr3_data$group,
  levels = c("Same-stop PTC+\n(3'UTR splicing)",
             "Diff-stop PTC+\n(own stop, inflated)",
             "Diff-stop PTC+\n(ref stop, corrected)",
             "NMD PTC-", "Control"))
utr3_n <- table(utr3_data$group)
```

PTC+ comparators are split by whether the strand-aware stop codon position is
the **same** as the reference or **different** (premature stop from frameshift
or in-frame stop in CDS). Stop codon position: `cds_stop` on + strand,
`cds_start` on - strand.

- **Same-stop PTC+** (`r fmt(utr3_n[[1]])`): The stop codon is the same as the
  reference. A 3'UTR splicing event repositioned the last EJC, making the
  existing stop >50 nt upstream of the new EJC. The 3'UTR length is correctly
  measured.
- **Diff-stop PTC+ (own stop)** (`r fmt(utr3_n[[2]])`): The stop codon moved
  upstream (PTC). The measured 3'UTR is inflated — it includes former CDS.
- **Diff-stop PTC+ (ref stop)** (`r fmt(utr3_n[[3]])`): Same pairs as above, but
  3'UTR is measured from the **reference's** stop codon position projected onto
  the comparator's exon structure. `r fmt(n_eligible)` of `r fmt(n_eligible + n_ineligible)`
  pairs were eligible (reference stop falls within comparator exons).
- **NMD PTC−** (`r fmt(utr3_n[[4]])`): No PTC. 3'UTR is correctly measured.
  *Example: GPAT3 — comp 3'UTR=1,108 bp, ref 3'UTR=1,108 bp.*
- **Control** (`r fmt(utr3_n[[5]])`): C4 comparators.
  *Example: SART1 — comp 3'UTR=1,107 bp, ref 3'UTR=1,107 bp.*

```{r goal3-fig6-utr3-density, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
pal5_utr3 <- c("Same-stop PTC+\n(3'UTR splicing)" = "#d6604d",
               "Diff-stop PTC+\n(own stop, inflated)" = "#fc8d59",
               "Diff-stop PTC+\n(ref stop, corrected)" = "#fee08b",
               "NMD PTC-" = "#d9ef8b",
               "Control" = "#67a9cf")

fig6 <- ggplot(utr3_data, aes(x = utr3_bp, fill = group)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal5_utr3) +
  labs(title = "3'UTR Length by PTC Mechanism",
       subtitle = "Correcting for CDS truncation reveals PTC-neg NMD isoforms have normal 3'UTR lengths",
       x = "3'UTR length (bp, log scale)", y = "Density", fill = "")
save_fig(fig6, "fig7_utr3_length_density", width = 10, height = 6)
```

## Table 7: 3'UTR Length Comparisons (Wilcoxon)

```{r goal3-table6-utr3-tests}
grps <- split(utr3_data$utr3_bp, utr3_data$group)

comparisons_list <- list(
  c("Same-stop PTC+\n(3'UTR splicing)", "Control"),
  c("Diff-stop PTC+\n(own stop, inflated)", "Control"),
  c("Diff-stop PTC+\n(ref stop, corrected)", "Control"),
  c("NMD PTC-", "Control"),
  c("Same-stop PTC+\n(3'UTR splicing)", "Diff-stop PTC+\n(ref stop, corrected)")
)

tests <- do.call(rbind, lapply(comparisons_list, function(pair) {
  g1 <- grps[[pair[1]]]
  g2 <- grps[[pair[2]]]
  wt <- wilcox.test(g1, g2)
  U <- as.numeric(wt$statistic)
  rbc <- 1 - (2 * U) / (length(g1) * length(g2))
  data.frame(
    group1 = gsub("\n", " ", pair[1]),
    n_group1 = length(g1), median_group1 = round(median(g1)),
    group2 = gsub("\n", " ", pair[2]),
    n_group2 = length(g2), median_group2 = round(median(g2)),
    median_diff_bp = round(median(g1) - median(g2)),
    rank_biserial_r = round(rbc, 3),
    p_value = signif(wt$p.value, 3),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

render_dt(tests, caption = "Table 7: 3'UTR Length Comparisons (Wilcoxon rank-sum test)")
write.csv(tests, file.path(table_dir, "table7_utr3_wilcoxon.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

Columns: **group1/group2** = the two groups being compared (see Figure 7 for
group definitions); **n_group1/n_group2** = number of isoforms in each group;
**median_group1/median_group2** = median 3'UTR length (bp);
**median_diff_bp** = difference in medians (group1 − group2);
**rank_biserial_r** = rank-biserial correlation (effect size; positive =
group1 longer); **p_value** = Wilcoxon rank-sum test p-value.

## Illustrative Example: 3'UTR Measurement Correction (CMAS)

The figure below shows the CMAS gene pair (reference ENST00000229329.7 vs NMD
comparator ENST00000534981.5) to illustrate the difference between the two
3'UTR measurements. The comparator has a skipped exon that causes a frameshift,
creating a PTC at genomic position 22,062,284. The reference stop codon is at
22,065,311.

```{r goal3-utr3-example, fig.width=10, fig.height=10}
# CMAS: + strand, ref has 8 exons, comp has 7 (skipped exon 22061281-22061452)
# Same CDS start (22046304), different stop (ref: 22065311, comp: 22062284)

ref_s <- c(22046218, 22055149, 22055455, 22058567, 22060832, 22061281, 22062281, 22065121)
ref_e <- c(22046563, 22055291, 22055610, 22058700, 22060926, 22061452, 22062434, 22065668)
comp_s <- c(22046225, 22055149, 22055455, 22058567, 22060832, 22062281, 22065121)
comp_e <- c(22046563, 22055291, 22055610, 22058700, 22060926, 22062434, 22065674)

# Skipped exon event (comparator lost exon 22061281-22061452)
se_event <- data.frame(
  five_prime = 22061281, three_prime = 22061452,
  event_type = "SE", direction = "LOSS")

# Annotations: PTC marker on comparator, reference stop marker on both
ptc_marker <- list(type = "ptc_marker", track = "comp",
  x = 22062284, label = "PTC", color = "#E74C3C")
ref_stop_marker <- list(type = "ptc_marker", track = "ref",
  x = 22065311, label = "Stop", color = "#27AE60")

# Panel A: "Own stop" — comparator CDS ends at PTC (22062284)
p1 <- plot_ucsc_pair(
  ref_s, ref_e, comp_s, comp_e, strand = "+",
  ref_cds = list(cds_start = 22046304, cds_stop = 22065311),
  comp_cds = list(cds_start = 22046304, cds_stop = 22062284),
  ref_label = "Reference (ENST00000229329.7)",
  comp_label = "NMD Comparator (ENST00000534981.5)",
  events = se_event,
  annotations = list(ptc_marker, ref_stop_marker),
  title = "A) 3'UTR at own stop (inflated)",
  subtitle = "Comparator CDS ends at PTC. Measured 3'UTR (thin) includes former CDS downstream of PTC.")

# Panel B: "Ref stop" — comparator CDS extends to reference stop (22065311)
ref_stop_comp <- list(type = "ptc_marker", track = "comp",
  x = 22065311, label = "Ref Stop", color = "#27AE60")

p2 <- plot_ucsc_pair(
  ref_s, ref_e, comp_s, comp_e, strand = "+",
  ref_cds = list(cds_start = 22046304, cds_stop = 22065311),
  comp_cds = list(cds_start = 22046304, cds_stop = 22065311),
  ref_label = "Reference (ENST00000229329.7)",
  comp_label = "NMD Comparator (ENST00000534981.5)",
  events = se_event,
  annotations = list(ptc_marker, ref_stop_marker, ref_stop_comp),
  title = "B) 3'UTR at reference stop (corrected)",
  subtitle = "Comparator CDS extended to reference stop. 3'UTR = only true downstream sequence.")

gridExtra::grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 1)
```

In panel A, the skipped exon (SE LOSS bracket) causes a frameshift that creates
a PTC (red triangle on comparator). The comparator's CDS (thick) ends at the
PTC, and everything downstream is measured as 3'UTR (thin) — inflating the
length. The reference stop codon (green triangle) is further downstream. In
panel B, the comparator's CDS boundary is set to the reference's stop position
(green triangle on both tracks), giving the "natural" 3'UTR length.

**Key finding (Figure 7, Table 7):** PTC-negative NMD comparators have 3'UTR lengths
indistinguishable from Control (p = `r signif(tests$p_value[tests$group1 == "NMD PTC-"], 2)`).
Long 3'UTR length does not appear to be an independent NMD trigger in this
dataset. The apparently long 3'UTRs in PTC+ isoforms are explained by two
mechanisms: (1) for same-stop PTC+ isoforms, the 3'UTR is genuinely extended by
the same splicing event that repositioned the EJC; (2) for diff-stop PTC+
isoforms, the 3'UTR measurement is inflated by inclusion of former CDS sequence
downstream of the premature stop.

## 3'UTR Splicing and NMD

The question is whether 3'UTR splicing contributes to NMD in our data,
and if so, through what mechanism — PTC creation (EJC repositioning) or a
PTC-independent pathway (e.g., long 3'UTR-mediated UPF1 recruitment).

```{r goal3-utr3-splicing}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: computed inline using count_utr3_splicing() defined in this chunk
# Methods: METHODS.md § "3'UTR Splicing Enrichment"
# Starting data: gene-matched C2 and C4 profiles (detailed_events from
#   Isopair::buildProfiles() → compareSplicingChoices) + cds.rds (Isopair::extractCds)

# Strand-aware stop codon position for 3'UTR event detection
# + strand: stop = cds_stop; - strand: stop = cds_start
cds_start_lookup_utr3 <- setNames(cds$cds_start, cds$isoform_id)
cds_stop_lookup_utr3  <- setNames(cds$cds_stop, cds$isoform_id)
strand_lookup <- setNames(cds$strand, cds$isoform_id)

count_utr3_splicing <- function(profiles, comp_id_subset = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(comp_id_subset)) {
    idx <- which(profiles$comparator_isoform_id %in% comp_id_subset)
  } else {
    idx <- seq_len(nrow(profiles))
  }
  n_with <- 0L
  n_total <- 0L
  for (i in idx) {
    comp_id <- profiles$comparator_isoform_id[i]
    de <- profiles$detailed_events[[i]]
    comp_strand <- strand_lookup[comp_id]
    comp_stop <- if (!is.na(comp_strand) && comp_strand == "-") {
      cds_start_lookup_utr3[comp_id]
    } else {
      cds_stop_lookup_utr3[comp_id]
    }
    if (is.na(comp_stop) || is.na(comp_strand)) next
    n_total <- n_total + 1L
    if (is.null(de) || nrow(de) == 0) next
    if (comp_strand == "+") {
      utr3_ev <- de[de$five_prime >= comp_stop | de$three_prime >= comp_stop, ]
    } else {
      utr3_ev <- de[de$five_prime <= comp_stop | de$three_prime <= comp_stop, ]
    }
    if (nrow(utr3_ev) > 0) n_with <- n_with + 1L
  }
  list(n_with = n_with, n_total = n_total,
       pct = round(100 * n_with / max(n_total, 1), 1))
}

prof_c4_as <- set_results[["c4_allsamples"]]$profiles

utr3_ptcneg <- count_utr3_splicing(prof_c2, ptc_neg_ids)
utr3_ptcpos <- count_utr3_splicing(prof_c2, ptc_pos_comp_ids)
utr3_ctrl   <- count_utr3_splicing(prof_c4_as)

ft_utr3_neg <- fisher.test(matrix(c(
  utr3_ptcneg$n_with, utr3_ptcneg$n_total - utr3_ptcneg$n_with,
  utr3_ctrl$n_with, utr3_ctrl$n_total - utr3_ctrl$n_with), nrow = 2))
ft_utr3_pos <- fisher.test(matrix(c(
  utr3_ptcpos$n_with, utr3_ptcpos$n_total - utr3_ptcpos$n_with,
  utr3_ctrl$n_with, utr3_ctrl$n_total - utr3_ctrl$n_with), nrow = 2))

utr3_summary <- data.frame(
  group = c("NMD PTC-", "NMD PTC+", "Control"),
  n_with_utr3_event = c(utr3_ptcneg$n_with, utr3_ptcpos$n_with, utr3_ctrl$n_with),
  n_total = c(utr3_ptcneg$n_total, utr3_ptcpos$n_total, utr3_ctrl$n_total),
  pct = c(utr3_ptcneg$pct, utr3_ptcpos$pct, utr3_ctrl$pct),
  vs_control_OR = c(round(as.numeric(ft_utr3_neg$estimate), 2),
                     round(as.numeric(ft_utr3_pos$estimate), 2), NA),
  vs_control_p = c(signif(ft_utr3_neg$p.value, 3),
                    signif(ft_utr3_pos$p.value, 3), NA))

kable(utr3_summary,
      caption = "3'UTR Splicing Prevalence by Group",
      col.names = c("Group", "With 3'UTR Event", "Total", "%",
                     "OR vs Control", "p vs Control"))
```

Columns: **Group**; **With 3'UTR Event** = pairs where ≥1 splice event has
coordinates in the 3'UTR (downstream of the strand-aware stop codon position);
**OR/p vs Control** = Fisher's exact test comparing to Control (C4).

```{r goal3-utr3-same-stop-verification}
# ── Direct verification: 3'UTR splicing creates PTCs via EJC repositioning ──
# For same-stop PTC+ pairs, the stop codon is identical to the reference.
# The PTC status arises because the comparator has more exon-exon junctions
# downstream of the stop codon (from 3'UTR splicing), repositioning the last EJC.
# We can verify by comparing n_downstream_ejcs between ref and comp.

same_stop_ps <- ptc_pos_ps[ptc_pos_ps$same_stop == TRUE, ]
ptc_ejc_lookup <- setNames(ptc$n_downstream_ejcs, ptc$isoform_id)

same_stop_ps$comp_ejcs <- ptc_ejc_lookup[same_stop_ps$comparator_isoform_id]
same_stop_ps$ref_ejcs <- ptc_ejc_lookup[same_stop_ps$reference_isoform_id]
same_stop_ps$ejc_diff <- same_stop_ps$comp_ejcs - same_stop_ps$ref_ejcs

n_comp_more_ejcs <- sum(same_stop_ps$ejc_diff > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
n_same_ejcs <- sum(same_stop_ps$ejc_diff == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
n_comp_fewer_ejcs <- sum(same_stop_ps$ejc_diff < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
n_valid <- sum(!is.na(same_stop_ps$ejc_diff))
```

### 3'UTR Splicing Creates PTCs via EJC Repositioning

Among the `r fmt(nrow(same_stop_ps))` same-stop PTC+ pairs (where the
comparator has the same stop codon as the reference but is classified as PTC+),
we directly verified the mechanism by comparing the number of exon-exon
junctions downstream of the stop codon:

- **`r n_comp_more_ejcs`** pairs (`r round(100 * n_comp_more_ejcs / n_valid, 1)`%):
  comparator has MORE downstream EJCs than reference — confirming that 3'UTR
  splicing added new junctions, repositioning the last EJC and creating the PTC
- **`r n_same_ejcs`** pairs: same number of downstream EJCs (PTC may arise from
  junction repositioning rather than addition)
- **`r n_comp_fewer_ejcs`** pairs: comparator has fewer EJCs (unexpected —
  may reflect annotation differences)

### Conclusions: 3'UTR Mechanisms in NMD

Three lines of evidence address whether 3'UTR length or splicing triggers
PTC-independent NMD:

1. **No NMD subgroup has substantially longer 3'UTRs than Control when measured
   from the appropriate stop codon** (Table 7). PTC-negative NMD comparators
   have the same median 3'UTR as Control (p =
   `r signif(tests$p_value[tests$group1 == "NMD PTC-"], 2)`). Same-stop PTC+
   comparators are also indistinguishable from Control (p =
   `r signif(tests$p_value[tests$group1 == "Same-stop PTC+ (3'UTR splicing)" & tests$group2 == "Control"], 2)`).
   The diff-stop PTC+ group measured at own stop has longer 3'UTRs (p < 10^-54^),
   but this is an artifact of measuring from the PTC rather than the true stop.
   When corrected using the reference stop position, the effect is small (median
   difference `r tests$median_diff_bp[tests$group1 == "Diff-stop PTC+ (ref stop, corrected)" & tests$group2 == "Control"]`
   bp, r = `r tests$rank_biserial_r[tests$group1 == "Diff-stop PTC+ (ref stop, corrected)" & tests$group2 == "Control"]`,
   p = `r signif(tests$p_value[tests$group1 == "Diff-stop PTC+ (ref stop, corrected)" & tests$group2 == "Control"], 2)`).

2. **3'UTR splicing that triggers NMD does so by creating PTCs** (EJC
   repositioning), not through a PTC-independent pathway. The
   `r fmt(nrow(same_stop_ps))` same-stop PTC+ pairs are direct evidence:
   `r round(100 * n_comp_more_ejcs / n_valid, 1)`% have additional downstream
   EJCs in the comparator from 3'UTR splicing events.

3. **3'UTR splicing prevalence** is actually **depleted** in PTC-negative NMD
   vs Control (OR =
   `r round(as.numeric(ft_utr3_neg$estimate), 2)`, p =
   `r signif(ft_utr3_neg$p.value, 3)`). This is consistent with our finding
   that 3'UTR splicing creates PTCs — isoforms that trigger NMD without a PTC
   would be expected to have *less* 3'UTR splicing, not more.

## 5'UTR uORF Analysis

Upstream open reading frames (uORFs) in the 5'UTR are a known mechanism that
can trigger NMD independently of PTCs in the main CDS. We scanned the 5'UTR
sequence of each comparator isoform for uORFs (AUG followed by an in-frame stop
codon, minimum 3 codons / 9 nt). uORFs whose stop codon falls at or beyond the
main CDS start are classified as **overlapping** — a particularly potent NMD
trigger.

```{r goal3-uorf}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source script: 05b_uorf_analysis.R → analysis_cache/uorf_analysis.rds
# Methods: METHODS.md § "5'UTR uORF Analysis"
#
# Pipeline:
#   1. 5'UTR boundaries computed by compute_utr5_length() in 05b_uorf_analysis.R
#      Input: genomic CDS coordinates (cds.rds) + exon structure (structures.rds)
#      + strand: CDS start = cds_start (plus) or cds_stop (minus)
#      Validation: 98.4% of isoforms have ATG at computed CDS start position
#   2. 5'UTR sequences extracted from SQANTI corrected transcript FASTA
#      (nmd_lungcells_corrected.fasta) via awk-based subset extraction
#   3. uORF detection by find_uorfs() in 05b_uorf_analysis.R:
#      gregexpr("ATG") finds all AUG positions in 5'UTR; for each, walks in-frame
#      through full transcript to first stop codon (TAA/TAG/TGA). Min 3 codons.
#      Overlapping uORFs: stop codon at or past main CDS start.
#   4. Groups: PTC_neg, PTC_pos, Control (same coding pair definitions as Goal 3)

uorf_data <- readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, "uorf_analysis.rds"))
uorf <- uorf_data$per_isoform
uorf$group <- factor(uorf$group, levels = c("PTC_neg", "PTC_pos", "Control"))
```

```{r goal3-uorf-summary}
uorf_summary <- uorf |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    median_utr5_bp = median(utr5_length),
    pct_with_uorf = round(100 * mean(n_uorfs > 0), 1),
    median_n_uorfs = median(n_uorfs),
    mean_n_uorfs = round(mean(n_uorfs), 1),
    pct_overlapping = round(100 * mean(n_overlapping_uorfs > 0), 1),
    .groups = "drop")

render_dt(uorf_summary, caption = "Table 8a: uORF Prevalence by Group")
```

Columns: **group** = PTC_neg (NMD without PTC), PTC_pos (NMD with PTC), or
Control (C4); **n** = number of isoforms; **median_utr5_bp** = median 5'UTR
length; **pct_with_uorf** = % with ≥1 uORF (≥3 codons); **median/mean_n_uorfs** =
uORFs per isoform; **pct_overlapping** = % with ≥1 overlapping uORF (stop
codon at or past CDS start).

```{r goal3-uorf-tests}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: uorf_data$per_isoform (from 05b_uorf_analysis.R)
# Methods: METHODS.md § "5'UTR uORF Analysis"
# Test: Fisher's exact test on 2x2 table (group × has_uorf) for each pair of groups
# "any uORF": isoform has ≥1 uORF (≥3 codons) in the 5'UTR
# "overlapping uORF": isoform has ≥1 uORF whose stop codon falls at or past CDS start
# n per group: PTC_neg=1,860, PTC_pos=1,458, Control=3,238

uorf_tests <- list()
test_pairs <- list(
  c("PTC_neg", "Control", "any uORF"),
  c("PTC_pos", "Control", "any uORF"),
  c("PTC_neg", "PTC_pos", "any uORF"),
  c("PTC_neg", "Control", "overlapping uORF")
)

for (tp in test_pairs) {
  sub <- uorf[uorf$group %in% tp[1:2], ]
  sub$group <- droplevels(factor(sub$group))
  if (tp[3] == "any uORF") {
    tbl <- table(sub$group, sub$n_uorfs > 0)
  } else {
    tbl <- table(sub$group, sub$n_overlapping_uorfs > 0)
  }
  ft <- tryCatch(fisher.test(tbl), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(ft)) {
    n1 <- sum(sub$group == tp[1])
    n2 <- sum(sub$group == tp[2])
    uorf_tests[[length(uorf_tests) + 1]] <- data.frame(
      comparison = paste(tp[1], "vs", tp[2]),
      test = tp[3],
      n_group1 = n1, n_group2 = n2,
      OR = round(as.numeric(ft$estimate), 2),
      p_value = signif(as.numeric(ft$p.value), 3),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
}
uorf_test_df <- do.call(rbind, uorf_tests)
render_dt(uorf_test_df, caption = "Table 8b: uORF Enrichment Tests (Fisher's exact)")
```

Columns: **comparison** = group pair tested; **test** = "any uORF" (≥1 uORF) or
"overlapping uORF" (≥1 uORF with stop at/past CDS start); **n_group1/n_group2** =
group sizes; **OR** = Fisher's exact test odds ratio; **p_value** = Fisher p-value.

## Figure 8: uORF Count Distribution

```{r goal3-uorf-density, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# Density plot (better than dodged histogram for different group sizes)
uorf_plot <- uorf[uorf$utr5_length > 0, ]
uorf_plot$group_label <- factor(uorf_plot$group,
  levels = c("PTC_neg", "PTC_pos", "Control"),
  labels = c("NMD PTC-", "NMD PTC+", "Control"))

fig_uorf <- ggplot(uorf_plot, aes(x = n_uorfs + 0.5, fill = group_label)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("NMD PTC-" = "#fddbc7", "NMD PTC+" = "#ef8a62",
                                "Control" = "#67a9cf")) +
  labs(title = "uORF Count Distribution by Group",
       subtitle = "PTC-negative NMD isoforms have dramatically more uORFs (median 8 vs 1 in Control)",
       x = "Number of uORFs (+0.5, log scale)", y = "Density", fill = "")
save_fig(fig_uorf, "fig8_uorf_count_distribution", width = 10, height = 6)
```

**Key finding:** PTC-negative NMD comparators have dramatically more uORFs than
Control (96.2% vs 63.3% with any uORF, OR =
`r uorf_test_df$OR[uorf_test_df$comparison == "PTC_neg vs Control" & uorf_test_df$test == "any uORF"]`,
p < 10^-180^). They also have longer 5'UTRs (median
`r uorf_summary$median_utr5_bp[uorf_summary$group == "PTC_neg"]` bp vs
`r uorf_summary$median_utr5_bp[uorf_summary$group == "Control"]` bp in Control),
which provides more sequence for uORFs. Overlapping uORFs (stop codon at or past
main CDS start) are also enriched (61.5% vs 27.9%, OR =
`r uorf_test_df$OR[uorf_test_df$comparison == "PTC_neg vs Control" & uorf_test_df$test == "overlapping uORF"]`).

Combined with the 3'UTR length finding (PTC-neg NMD isoforms have normal 3'UTR
lengths), this points to **5'UTR uORFs as the dominant non-PTC NMD mechanism**
in this dataset, rather than long 3'UTR-mediated NMD.

**Caveat:** The high uORF count is partly driven by longer 5'UTRs (more sequence =
more chance of ATG + in-frame stop). The enrichment should be interpreted in
conjunction with the 5'UTR length difference.

```{r goal3-uorf-by-frame-tests}
# Wilcoxon test: 5'UTR length PTC_neg vs Control, per frame category
uorf_fc_tests <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(uorf_by_fc$frame_label), function(fc) {
  neg <- uorf_by_fc$utr5_length[uorf_by_fc$frame_label == fc & uorf_by_fc$group_label == "NMD PTC-"]
  ctrl <- uorf_by_fc$utr5_length[uorf_by_fc$frame_label == fc & uorf_by_fc$group_label == "Control"]
  if (length(neg) < 5 || length(ctrl) < 5) return(NULL)
  wt <- wilcox.test(neg, ctrl)
  data.frame(
    frame_category = fc,
    n_ptc_neg = length(neg), median_ptc_neg = round(median(neg)),
    n_control = length(ctrl), median_control = round(median(ctrl)),
    wilcox_p = signif(wt$p.value, 3),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

kable(uorf_fc_tests, caption = "Table 8d: 5'UTR Length — PTC-neg vs Control by Frame Category (Wilcoxon)")
```

Columns: **frame_category**; **n_ptc_neg/n_control** = group sizes;
**median_ptc_neg/median_control** = median 5'UTR length (bp);
**wilcox_p** = Wilcoxon rank-sum test p-value.

The **diff-start same-frame** PTC-negative NMD isoforms are the primary drivers
of the uORF enrichment: 99.1% have uORFs (median 9) with a median 5'UTR of
779 bp, compared to 81.9% (median 4, 5'UTR 446 bp) in Control. This is
consistent with the use of an alternative downstream start codon: the original
start codon becomes a uORF in the extended 5'UTR, and translation from the
downstream AUG produces the same reading frame but a shorter protein. The
resulting overlapping uORF (from the original AUG) is a potent NMD trigger.

**Limitations:** uORF detection is sequence-based and does not confirm
translation. Not all sequence-predicted uORFs are functional NMD triggers.
Other non-PTC NMD mechanisms (3'UTR secondary structure, EJC-independent UPF1
recruitment) cannot be ruled out from structural data alone.

## Cumulative NMD Mechanism Attribution

```{r goal4-cumulative-attribution, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Synthesizes across Goals 2-4 to provide a single accounting of NMD mechanisms.
# All counts derive from coding_pairs_c2 (gene-matched coding NMD pairs).
# PTC+/PTC-: from goal3-identify-ptc-neg (coding_pairs_c2$comp_has_ptc)
# Same-stop/diff-stop: from goal3-fig6-pop (strand-aware stop comparison)
# Frameshift/in-frame: from goal2-ptc-mechanisms (frame_category)

n_coding_total <- nrow(coding_pairs_c2)
n_same_stop <- length(same_stop_ids)
n_diff_stop <- length(diff_stop_ids)

n_diffstop_fs <- sum(ptc_plus$comparator_isoform_id %in% diff_stop_ids &
                       ptc_plus$is_frameshift_cat)
n_diffstop_inframe <- length(diff_stop_ids) - n_diffstop_fs

# ── Flowchart: NMD mechanism hierarchy ──
# Using DiagrammeR for a top-down flowchart
library(DiagrammeR)

grViz(sprintf('
digraph nmd_flowchart {
  graph [rankdir=TB, fontname="Helvetica", nodesep=0.6, ranksep=0.8]
  node [shape=box, style="filled,rounded", fontname="Helvetica", fontsize=12,
        width=2.5, height=0.6]

  all [label="All NMD+ coding pairs\\n%s", fillcolor="#f0f0f0"]

  ptc_pos [label="PTC+\\n%s (%s%%)", fillcolor="#fee0d2"]
  ptc_neg [label="PTC-\\n%s (%s%%)", fillcolor="#deebf7"]

  same_stop [label="Same stop codon\\n(3-prime UTR splice)\\n%s (%s%%)",
             fillcolor="#fc9272"]
  new_stop  [label="New stop codon\\n%s (%s%%)", fillcolor="#fc9272"]

  fs_new    [label="Frameshift-induced\\n%s (%s%%)", fillcolor="#fb6a4a"]
  if_new    [label="In-frame splice event\\n%s (%s%%)", fillcolor="#fb6a4a"]

  all -> ptc_pos
  all -> ptc_neg
  ptc_pos -> same_stop
  ptc_pos -> new_stop
  new_stop -> fs_new
  new_stop -> if_new
}',
  fmt(n_coding_total),
  fmt(n_ptc_pos), round(100 * n_ptc_pos / n_coding_total, 1),
  fmt(n_ptc_neg), round(100 * n_ptc_neg / n_coding_total, 1),
  fmt(n_same_stop), round(100 * n_same_stop / n_coding_total, 1),
  fmt(n_diff_stop), round(100 * n_diff_stop / n_coding_total, 1),
  fmt(n_diffstop_fs), round(100 * n_diffstop_fs / n_coding_total, 1),
  fmt(n_diffstop_inframe), round(100 * n_diffstop_inframe / n_coding_total, 1)
))
```

The flowchart shows the complete hierarchy for `r fmt(n_coding_total)` coding
gene-matched NMD pairs. The PTC+ branch (`r fmt(n_ptc_pos)` pairs,
`r round(100 * n_ptc_pos / n_coding_total, 1)`%) represents definitive
structural mechanisms: for each pair we identify the specific splice event
responsible (Figure 6). The PTC- branch (`r fmt(n_ptc_neg)` pairs,
`r round(100 * n_ptc_neg / n_coding_total, 1)`%) lacks individual-level
causal attribution, but shows group-level enrichment for 5'UTR uORFs
(Figure 8, Tables 8a-8d) and no evidence for 3'UTR length as an independent
trigger (Table 7).

**PTC+: New stop codon** (`r fmt(n_diff_stop)`,
`r round(100 * n_diff_stop / n_coding_total, 1)`%): A splice event introduces
a premature stop codon not present in the reference. Subdivides into
frameshift-induced (`r fmt(n_diffstop_fs)`) — a splice event shifts the reading
frame, and the new frame encounters a stop — and in-frame splice events
(`r fmt(n_diffstop_inframe)`) — the event directly introduces an in-frame stop
codon.

**PTC+: Same stop / 3'UTR splice** (`r fmt(n_same_stop)`,
`r round(100 * n_same_stop / n_coding_total, 1)`%): The comparator and
reference share the same stop codon. A 3'UTR splicing event repositions an EJC
>50 nt downstream, making the normal stop "premature" under the EJC model.

**PTC-** (`r fmt(n_ptc_neg)`,
`r round(100 * n_ptc_neg / n_coding_total, 1)`%): No individual causal
attribution. As a group, PTC-negative NMD comparators have longer 5'UTRs
(median `r uorf_summary$median_utr5_bp[uorf_summary$group == "PTC_neg"]` bp vs
`r uorf_summary$median_utr5_bp[uorf_summary$group == "Control"]` bp in Control)
and more uORFs (median `r uorf_summary$median_n_uorfs[uorf_summary$group == "PTC_neg"]` vs
`r uorf_summary$median_n_uorfs[uorf_summary$group == "Control"]`; OR =
`r round(1 / uorf_test_df$OR[uorf_test_df$comparison == "PTC_neg vs Control" & uorf_test_df$test == "any uORF"], 1)`,
p < 10^-180^), consistent with uORF-mediated NMD. Overlapping uORFs have been
shown to strongly repress main ORF expression through a combination of NMD and
translational inhibition (Luo & Bhalla 2018), and uORF-containing transcripts
are enriched among NMD targets (Nyikó et al. 2009; Ow et al. 2023). However,
the relative contribution of NMD vs translational repression has not been
cleanly separated, and individual attribution is not possible from sequence
data alone.


# 5. Protein-Level Consequences of Normal Alternative Splicing {#goal5}

**Goal:** When a cell uses its second-most-abundant isoform instead of the
dominant one, how different is the protein? This section examines the dominant vs
next-best non-NMD isoform for each gene. Unlike Goals 1-4 (gene-matched NMD vs
Control), this uses **all non-NMD isoform comparisons** — every gene with ≥2
non-NMD isoforms, deduplicated across cell types.

## Analysis Overview

```{r goal5-load}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: 05f_protein_analysis_v2.R → protein_analysis_v2.rds
# Pipeline:
#   1. All coding C4 isoform comparisons (unmatched), deduplicated
#   2. Isopair::mapSpliceToProtein() → protein-level regions per splice event
#   3. hmmscan (Pfam-A) → domain positions on each isoform's protein sequence
#   4. Domain-event intersection → disrupted/gained classification
#   5. Isopair::testDomainEnrichment() → Fisher's test vs reference prevalence
#   6. PeptideAtlas → mass-spec validation of splice-specific peptides

prot_v2 <- readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, "protein_analysis_v2.rds"))
pe <- prot_v2$protein_events
dom <- prot_v2$domain_effects
parsed_doms <- prot_v2$parsed_doms  # per-isoform hmmscan domain annotations

# Mass-spec: use the quality-enriched reanalysis (massspec_peptideatlas_v2.rds)
# as the single source of truth. prot_v2$massspec is from the initial run and
# has slightly different hit counts due to PeptideAtlas version differences.
ms <- readRDS(file.path(cache_dir, "massspec_peptideatlas_v2.rds"))

# Key counts (single source of truth for this section)
n_total       <- prot_v2$metadata$n_unique_pairs
n_with_events <- length(unique(paste(pe$reference_isoform_id, pe$comparator_isoform_id)))
n_events      <- nrow(pe)
n_dom_overlaps <- nrow(dom)
n_unique_doms  <- length(unique(dom$pfam_acc))
n_disrupted   <- length(unique(paste(dom$comparator_isoform_id[dom$effect == "disrupted_lost"],
                                      dom$reference_isoform_id[dom$effect == "disrupted_lost"])))
n_gained      <- length(unique(paste(dom$comparator_isoform_id[dom$effect == "gained_intact"],
                                      dom$reference_isoform_id[dom$effect == "gained_intact"])))
n_with_domains <- length(unique(paste(dom$comparator_isoform_id, dom$reference_isoform_id)))
n_overrep_tested <- nrow(prot_v2$overrep_tests)
n_overrep_sig    <- sum(prot_v2$overrep_tests$significant, na.rm = TRUE)
n_ms_queried  <- nrow(ms)
n_ms_hits     <- sum(ms$n_pa_hits > 0)
n_peptides    <- sum(ms$n_novel_peptides)
n_pep_hits    <- sum(ms$n_pa_hits)

# Pair keys for joining pe/dom/ms
pe$pair_key  <- paste(pe$reference_isoform_id, pe$comparator_isoform_id, sep = "|")
dom$pair_key <- paste(dom$reference_isoform_id, dom$comparator_isoform_id, sep = "|")
# ms already has pair_key from 05f_protein_analysis_v2.R

# MS hit lookup (pair keys with ≥1 PeptideAtlas hit)
ms_hit_keys <- ms$pair_key[ms$n_pa_hits > 0]

# Gene symbol annotation for ms
gene_lk <- setNames(pe$gene_id, pe$comparator_isoform_id)
gene_lk <- gene_lk[!duplicated(names(gene_lk))]
ms$gene_id <- gene_lk[ms$comparator_isoform_id]
ms$gene_symbol <- gene_symbol_lookup[ms$gene_id]
ms_hits <- ms[ms$n_pa_hits > 0, ]

# Cell-type membership (protein analysis uses lowercase labels)
ct_membership <- prot_v2$ct_membership
ct_map <- c(AT = "at", DD = "dd", DO = "do", FB = "fb", MV = "mv")
```

The unit tracked through this section is always **isoform comparisons** (one per
gene: dominant vs next-best non-NMD isoform).

```{r goal5-flowchart}

dom_pair_keys <- unique(dom$pair_key)
n_dom_with_ms <- sum(dom_pair_keys %in% ms_hit_keys)

# C4 pairs in all_samples (unique, no CT duplication)
n_c4_allsamples <- nrow(readRDS(file.path("data_mashr", "profiles_c4_allsamples.rds")))

dot_g5 <- sprintf('

  Z [label=<<b>%s Non-NMD Isoforms</b> (from Section 0)<br/>→ C4 pairs: top 2 non-NMD isoforms per gene<br/>%s unique pairs in all_samples>,

     fillcolor="#e8f4f8", color="#2c7fb8"]

     fillcolor="#fff7bc", color="#d95f0e"]
  D [label=<<b>%s / %s Domains Over-Represented</b><br/>(FDR &lt; 0.05 vs reference prevalence)>,
     fillcolor="#c7e9c0", color="#31a354"]
  E [label=<<b>%s Domain-Affected Pairs Have Mass-Spec Support</b><br/>(splice-specific peptide in PeptideAtlas)>,
     fillcolor="#dadaeb", color="#6a51a3"]
  F [label=<<b>Cell-Type-Specific Analysis</b><br/>(domain overlap by CT, direction × CT interaction)>,
     fillcolor="#fde0dd", color="#c51b8a"]

  Z -> A [label="  pool CTs, coding filter, dedup", fontsize=22, fontname="Helvetica"]
  A -> B -> C -> D
  C -> E
  B -> F
}',
  fmt(n_nonnmd_as),
  fmt(n_c4_allsamples),

  fmt(n_with_domains), fmt(n_disrupted), fmt(n_gained),
  fmt(n_overrep_sig), fmt(n_overrep_tested),
  fmt(n_dom_with_ms))

DiagrammeR::grViz(dot_g5, width = 1200, height = 1100)
```

## Figure 10: Domain Effects of Alternative Splicing

Of `r fmt(n_total)` coding isoform comparisons, `r fmt(n_with_events)`
(`r round(100 * n_with_events / n_total, 1)`%) have ≥1 CDS-overlapping splice
event. Among those, `r fmt(n_with_domains)` (`r round(100 * n_with_domains / n_total, 1)`%
of total) overlap ≥1 Pfam domain, with `r fmt(n_disrupted)` disrupted and
`r fmt(n_gained)` gained.

```{r goal5-domain-bar, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
n_both <- length(intersect(
  unique(paste(dom$comparator_isoform_id[dom$effect == "disrupted_lost"],
               dom$reference_isoform_id[dom$effect == "disrupted_lost"])),
  unique(paste(dom$comparator_isoform_id[dom$effect == "gained_intact"],
               dom$reference_isoform_id[dom$effect == "gained_intact"]))))

bar_data <- data.frame(
  category = c("No CDS-overlapping events",
               "CDS event, no domain overlap",
               "Both disrupted & gained",
               "Gained only",
               "Disrupted/lost only"),
  n = c(n_total - n_with_events,
        n_with_events - n_with_domains,
        n_both,
        n_gained - n_both,
        n_disrupted - n_both))
bar_data$pct <- round(100 * bar_data$n / n_total, 1)
bar_data$category <- factor(bar_data$category, levels = bar_data$category)
bar_data$label <- sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", format(bar_data$n, big.mark = ","), bar_data$pct)

ggplot(bar_data, aes(x = category, y = n, fill = category)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), hjust = -0.1, size = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Disrupted/lost only" = "#d6604d",
    "Gained only" = "#4393c3",
    "Both disrupted & gained" = "#8856a7",
    "CDS event, no domain overlap" = "#bdbdbd",
    "No CDS-overlapping events" = "#f0f0f0")) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.3))) +
  labs(title = "Domain Effects of Alternative Splicing",
       subtitle = sprintf("Denominator: %s coding isoform comparisons. Categories are mutually exclusive.",
                           fmt(n_total)),
       x = "", y = "Number of Isoform Comparisons") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  coord_flip()
```

pooled_summary <- data.frame(
