## Event-Level Gating: GAIN vs LOSS Domain Overlap

GAIN and LOSS events may interact differently with protein domains. A LOSS event
removes sequence from the comparator, potentially **disrupting** an existing
domain. A GAIN event adds sequence, potentially **introducing** an intact domain
that the reference lacks.

```{r goal5-direction-gating}
# ── Data provenance ──
# pe = prot_v2$protein_events (CDS-overlapping splice events, has direction column)
# dom = prot_v2$domain_effects (domain-event overlaps, has effect column)
# Join: pe events → dom overlaps via (reference_isoform_id, comparator_isoform_id,
#        event_type, event_protein_start/protein_start_aa, event_protein_end/protein_end_aa)

# Create event key for pe
pe$event_key <- paste(pe$reference_isoform_id, pe$comparator_isoform_id,
                      pe$event_type, pe$protein_start_aa, pe$protein_end_aa,
                      sep = "|")

# Create matching key for dom
dom$event_key <- paste(dom$reference_isoform_id, dom$comparator_isoform_id,
                       dom$event_type, dom$event_protein_start, dom$event_protein_end,
                       sep = "|")

# Flag each pe event as overlapping any domain or not
pe$has_domain_overlap <- pe$event_key %in% dom$event_key

# Separate by direction
gain_events <- pe[pe$direction == "GAIN", ]
loss_events <- pe[pe$direction == "LOSS", ]

n_gain <- nrow(gain_events)
n_loss <- nrow(loss_events)
n_gain_dom <- sum(gain_events$has_domain_overlap)
n_loss_dom <- sum(loss_events$has_domain_overlap)
pct_gain_dom <- round(100 * n_gain_dom / n_gain, 1)
pct_loss_dom <- round(100 * n_loss_dom / n_loss, 1)

# Fisher's exact test: domain overlap rate for GAIN vs LOSS
ft_direction <- fisher.test(matrix(c(n_gain_dom, n_gain - n_gain_dom,
                                     n_loss_dom, n_loss - n_loss_dom), nrow = 2))
```

GAIN events overlap at least one Pfam domain at a rate of **`r pct_gain_dom`%**
(`r fmt(n_gain_dom)` / `r fmt(n_gain)`), compared to **`r pct_loss_dom`%**
(`r fmt(n_loss_dom)` / `r fmt(n_loss)`) for LOSS events (Fisher's exact OR =
`r round(ft_direction$estimate, 2)`, p = `r signif(ft_direction$p.value, 3)`).
GAIN events preferentially target domain-containing protein regions.

### Figure 11: Domain Overlap Rate by Direction

```{r goal5-direction-bar, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
dir_bar <- data.frame(
  direction = c("GAIN", "LOSS"),
  pct = c(pct_gain_dom, pct_loss_dom),
  n = c(n_gain, n_loss),
  n_dom = c(n_gain_dom, n_loss_dom))
dir_bar$label <- sprintf("%.1f%%\n(%s / %s)", dir_bar$pct,
                          fmt(dir_bar$n_dom), fmt(dir_bar$n))

fig11 <- ggplot(dir_bar, aes(x = direction, y = pct, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), vjust = -0.3, size = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(GAIN = "#4393c3", LOSS = "#d6604d")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(dir_bar$pct) * 1.25),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  labs(title = "Domain Overlap Rate by Splice Event Direction",
       subtitle = sprintf("Fisher OR = %.2f, p = %s. Total events: %s GAIN, %s LOSS.",
                           ft_direction$estimate, signif(ft_direction$p.value, 3),
                           fmt(n_gain), fmt(n_loss)),
       x = "Event Direction", y = "% of Events Overlapping ≥1 Pfam Domain") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

save_fig(fig11, "fig11_domain_overlap_by_direction")
```

## Domain Enrichment by Direction

The following tables test which specific Pfam domains are over-represented
among disrupted and gained effects, and compare the two.

### Table 9: Disrupted Domain Enrichment

```{r goal5-enrichment}
# ── Data provenance ──
# overrep = prot_v2$overrep_tests (Fisher enrichment of disrupted domains)
# MS annotation: count disrupted pairs per domain that also have PeptideAtlas support
overrep <- prot_v2$overrep_tests

# Add MS support columns
disrupted_dom <- dom[dom$effect == "disrupted_lost", ]
disrupted_ms <- disrupted_dom |>
  dplyr::group_by(pfam_acc) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_ms_supported = dplyr::n_distinct(pair_key[pair_key %in% ms_hit_keys]),
    .groups = "drop")
overrep <- merge(overrep, disrupted_ms, by = "pfam_acc", all.x = TRUE)
overrep$n_ms_supported[is.na(overrep$n_ms_supported)] <- 0L
overrep$pct_ms <- round(100 * overrep$n_ms_supported / pmax(overrep$n_disrupted, 1), 1)

overrep_sig <- overrep[overrep$significant == TRUE & !is.na(overrep$significant), ]
overrep_sig <- overrep_sig[order(overrep_sig$fisher_p), ]
overrep_top <- head(overrep_sig, 30)
overrep_top$fisher_OR <- round(overrep_top$fisher_OR, 2)
overrep_top$padj <- signif(overrep_top$padj, 3)

render_dt(overrep_top[, c("pfam_acc", "domain_name", "n_ref", "n_disrupted",
  "n_ms_supported", "pct_ms", "fisher_OR", "padj")],
  caption = "Table 9: Top 30 Over-Represented Disrupted Domains (FDR < 0.05)")
```

Of `r fmt(n_overrep_tested)` Pfam domains tested, **`r fmt(n_overrep_sig)` are
significantly over-represented** among disrupted domains (FDR < 0.05). The test
compares each domain's disruption rate to its prevalence among reference
(dominant) isoforms.

Columns: **pfam_acc** = Pfam accession; **domain_name**; **n_ref** = reference
isoforms with this domain; **n_disrupted** = comparisons where this domain
overlaps a splice event; **n_ms_supported** = disrupted pairs with ≥1
PeptideAtlas hit for splice-specific peptides; **pct_ms** = % of disrupted pairs
with MS support; **fisher_OR** = odds ratio; **padj** = BH-adjusted p-value.

### Table 9b: Gained Domain Enrichment

```{r goal5-gained-enrichment}
# ── Data provenance ──
# dom$effect == "gained_intact": events where a GAIN introduces a domain
# Denominator: comparator-side domain prevalence from parsed_doms (hmmscan)
# n_total: total unique coding pairs (from prot_v2$metadata$n_unique_pairs)
# MS annotation: count gained pairs per domain that also have PeptideAtlas support

gained <- dom[dom$effect == "gained_intact", ]
gained_counts <- gained |>
  dplyr::group_by(pfam_acc) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_gained = dplyr::n_distinct(paste(reference_isoform_id, comparator_isoform_id)),
    domain_name = domain_name[1],
    .groups = "drop")

n_any_gained <- length(unique(paste(
  gained$reference_isoform_id, gained$comparator_isoform_id)))

# Add MS support columns
gained_ms <- gained |>
  dplyr::group_by(pfam_acc) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_ms_supported = dplyr::n_distinct(pair_key[pair_key %in% ms_hit_keys]),
    .groups = "drop")

# Comparator-side domain prevalence: how many comparator isoforms carry each domain?
comp_ids <- unique(pe$comparator_isoform_id)
comp_dom_counts <- parsed_doms[parsed_doms$isoform_id %in% comp_ids, ] |>
  dplyr::group_by(pfam_acc) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n_comp = dplyr::n_distinct(isoform_id), .groups = "drop")

gained_enrich <- merge(gained_counts, comp_dom_counts, by = "pfam_acc", all.x = TRUE)
gained_enrich$n_comp[is.na(gained_enrich$n_comp)] <- 0L
gained_enrich <- merge(gained_enrich, gained_ms, by = "pfam_acc", all.x = TRUE)
gained_enrich$n_ms_supported[is.na(gained_enrich$n_ms_supported)] <- 0L
gained_enrich$pct_ms <- round(100 * gained_enrich$n_ms_supported /
                                pmax(gained_enrich$n_gained, 1), 1)

# Fisher's exact test per domain
# 2×2: (gained / not gained) × (has domain / no domain)
# Denominator: comparator isoforms with this domain (n_comp)
gained_enrich$fisher_p <- NA_real_
gained_enrich$fisher_OR <- NA_real_
for (i in seq_len(nrow(gained_enrich))) {
  a <- gained_enrich$n_gained[i]
  b <- max(gained_enrich$n_comp[i] - a, 0L)
  c_val <- max(n_any_gained - a, 0L)
  d_val <- max(n_total - a - b - c_val, 0L)
  ft <- tryCatch(fisher.test(matrix(c(a, c_val, b, d_val), nrow = 2)),
                 error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(ft)) {
    gained_enrich$fisher_p[i] <- ft$p.value
    gained_enrich$fisher_OR[i] <- as.numeric(ft$estimate)
  }
}
gained_enrich$padj <- p.adjust(gained_enrich$fisher_p, method = "BH")
gained_enrich$significant <- gained_enrich$padj < 0.05
gained_enrich <- gained_enrich[order(gained_enrich$fisher_p), ]

n_gained_tested <- nrow(gained_enrich)
n_gained_sig <- sum(gained_enrich$significant, na.rm = TRUE)

gained_sig <- gained_enrich[gained_enrich$significant == TRUE &
                              !is.na(gained_enrich$significant), ]
gained_top <- head(gained_sig, 30)
gained_top$fisher_OR <- round(gained_top$fisher_OR, 2)
gained_top$padj <- signif(gained_top$padj, 3)

render_dt(gained_top[, c("pfam_acc", "domain_name", "n_comp", "n_gained",
  "n_ms_supported", "pct_ms", "fisher_OR", "padj")],
  caption = "Table 9b: Top 30 Over-Represented Gained Domains (FDR < 0.05)")
```

Of `r fmt(n_gained_tested)` Pfam domains tested, **`r fmt(n_gained_sig)` are
significantly over-represented** among gained-intact domains (FDR < 0.05). The
test compares each domain's rate of being gained intact to its prevalence among
comparator isoforms (the isoforms that carry the gained domain).

Columns: **pfam_acc** = Pfam accession; **domain_name**; **n_comp** = comparator
isoforms carrying this domain (baseline prevalence); **n_gained** = comparisons
where this domain is gained intact; **n_ms_supported** = gained pairs with ≥1
PeptideAtlas hit; **pct_ms** = % of gained pairs with MS support;
**fisher_OR** = odds ratio; **padj** = BH-adjusted p-value.

### Table 9c: Disrupted vs Gained Comparison

```{r goal5-disrupted-vs-gained}
# ── Data provenance ──
# For each domain with ≥5 affected pairs (disrupted or gained):
# Test whether the gained fraction exceeds the overall baseline.
# Baseline = overall gained fraction across all domain-affected pairs.

# Merge disrupted and gained counts
dg_compare <- merge(
  overrep[, c("pfam_acc", "domain_name", "n_disrupted")],
  gained_counts[, c("pfam_acc", "n_gained")],
  by = "pfam_acc", all = TRUE)
dg_compare$n_disrupted[is.na(dg_compare$n_disrupted)] <- 0L
dg_compare$n_gained[is.na(dg_compare$n_gained)] <- 0L

# Fill domain_name from gained_counts where missing
missing_name <- is.na(dg_compare$domain_name)
if (any(missing_name)) {
  name_lk <- setNames(gained_counts$domain_name, gained_counts$pfam_acc)
  dg_compare$domain_name[missing_name] <- name_lk[dg_compare$pfam_acc[missing_name]]
}

dg_compare$n_total_affected <- dg_compare$n_disrupted + dg_compare$n_gained
dg_compare$pct_gained <- round(100 * dg_compare$n_gained / dg_compare$n_total_affected, 1)

# Filter to domains with ≥5 affected pairs
dg_testable <- dg_compare[dg_compare$n_total_affected >= 5, ]

# Overall baseline: fraction of all domain effects that are gained
baseline_gained <- n_any_gained / (n_any_gained +
  length(unique(paste(
    dom$comparator_isoform_id[dom$effect == "disrupted_lost"],
    dom$reference_isoform_id[dom$effect == "disrupted_lost"]))))

# One-sided binomial test per domain: is gained fraction > baseline?
dg_testable$binom_p <- NA_real_
for (i in seq_len(nrow(dg_testable))) {
  bt <- tryCatch(
    binom.test(dg_testable$n_gained[i], dg_testable$n_total_affected[i],
               p = baseline_gained, alternative = "greater"),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(bt)) dg_testable$binom_p[i] <- bt$p.value
}
dg_testable$padj <- p.adjust(dg_testable$binom_p, method = "BH")
dg_testable$significant <- dg_testable$padj < 0.05
dg_testable <- dg_testable[order(-dg_testable$pct_gained), ]

n_dg_tested <- nrow(dg_testable)
n_dg_sig <- sum(dg_testable$significant, na.rm = TRUE)

dg_display <- dg_testable[, c("pfam_acc", "domain_name", "n_disrupted",
  "n_gained", "n_total_affected", "pct_gained", "padj")]
dg_display$padj <- signif(dg_display$padj, 3)

render_dt(dg_display,
  caption = sprintf("Table 9c: Disrupted vs Gained by Domain (≥5 affected pairs, baseline gained = %.1f%%)",
                    100 * baseline_gained))
```

Of `r fmt(n_dg_tested)` domains with ≥5 affected pairs, **`r fmt(n_dg_sig)`**
have a gained fraction significantly above the overall baseline of
**`r round(100 * baseline_gained, 1)`%** (one-sided binomial, BH-adjusted
p < 0.05).

Columns: **pfam_acc** = Pfam accession; **domain_name**; **n_disrupted** =
pairs where the domain is disrupted; **n_gained** = pairs where the domain is
gained intact; **n_total_affected** = disrupted + gained; **pct_gained** =
percentage gained; **padj** = BH-adjusted binomial p-value.

## Mass Spectrometry Integration

Domain overlap results are cross-referenced with PeptideAtlas mass-spectrometry
data to assess whether domain-affecting splice events produce detectable protein
products.

### Table 10: Domain × Mass-Spec Cross-Tabulation

```{r goal5-domain-ms-crosstab}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Universe: pairs with CDS-overlapping events (n_with_events)
# dom$pair_key: pairs with domain overlap
# ms_hit_keys: pairs with ≥1 PeptideAtlas hit (from ms loaded in goal5-load)
# 2×2: (domain affected / not) × (MS hit / not)

cds_pair_keys <- unique(pe$pair_key)
has_dom <- cds_pair_keys %in% dom_pair_keys
has_ms  <- cds_pair_keys %in% ms_hit_keys

a <- sum(has_dom & has_ms)
b <- sum(has_dom & !has_ms)
c_val <- sum(!has_dom & has_ms)
d_val <- sum(!has_dom & !has_ms)

ft_dom_ms <- fisher.test(matrix(c(a, c_val, b, d_val), nrow = 2))

crosstab <- data.frame(
  category = c("Domain affected", "No domain affected", "Total"),
  ms_hit = c(a, c_val, a + c_val),
  no_ms_hit = c(b, d_val, b + d_val),
  total = c(a + b, c_val + d_val, a + b + c_val + d_val))

kable(crosstab,
  caption = "Table 10: Domain × Mass-Spec Cross-Tabulation",
  col.names = c("", "MS Hit", "No MS Hit", "Total"))
```

Among `r fmt(n_with_events)` pairs with CDS-overlapping events,
domain-affected pairs have a mass-spec hit rate of
**`r round(100 * a / (a + b), 1)`%** vs **`r round(100 * c_val / (c_val + d_val), 1)`%**
for pairs without domain overlap (Fisher OR =
`r round(ft_dom_ms$estimate, 2)`, p = `r signif(ft_dom_ms$p.value, 3)`).

Columns: **MS Hit** = pairs with ≥1 PeptideAtlas-confirmed splice-specific
peptide; **No MS Hit** = no PeptideAtlas match; rows stratified by whether the
pair has ≥1 Pfam domain affected by alternative splicing.

### Mass-Spec Validation Summary

```{r goal5-massspec-summary}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Source: massspec_peptideatlas_v2.rds loaded in goal5-load chunk (single source of truth)
# Pipeline: splice-specific peptides from event-affected protein regions
#   → exact match against Human PeptideAtlas 2024-01 (1.5M peptides with
#   n_observations, n_samples, best_probability per peptide)

ms_summary <- data.frame(
  metric = c("Comparisons with splice-specific peptides",
             "Comparisons with ≥1 PeptideAtlas hit",
             "  — with ≥2 confirmed peptides",
             "  — with ≥4 confirmed peptides",
             "  — high-confidence (best peptide in ≥10 samples)",
             "Total splice-specific peptides queried",
             "Total peptides found in PeptideAtlas"),
  n = c(n_ms_queried, n_ms_hits,
        sum(ms_hits$n_pa_hits >= 2),
        sum(ms_hits$n_pa_hits >= 4),
        sum(ms_hits$max_n_samples >= 10),
        n_peptides, n_pep_hits),
  pct_of_queried = c(NA, round(100 * n_ms_hits / n_ms_queried, 1),
        round(100 * sum(ms_hits$n_pa_hits >= 2) / n_ms_queried, 1),
        round(100 * sum(ms_hits$n_pa_hits >= 4) / n_ms_queried, 1),
        round(100 * sum(ms_hits$max_n_samples >= 10) / n_ms_queried, 1),
        NA, round(100 * n_pep_hits / n_peptides, 1)))

kable(ms_summary, caption = "Table 10a: Mass Spectrometry Validation Summary",
      col.names = c("Metric", "N", "% of queried"))
```

Columns: **Metric**; **N** = count; **% of queried** = percentage of the
`r fmt(n_ms_queried)` comparisons with splice-specific peptides (first block)
or of total peptides (last row).

## Cell-Type Domain Analysis

The analyses above use deduplicated pairs pooled across cell types. Here we
stratify by cell type to assess whether domain overlap patterns vary across
the five lung cell populations. Pairs appear in all cell types where they were
observed, so cell types are **not independent** — a pair shared across three
CTs contributes to each. This inflates per-CT sample sizes; interpret
cross-CT comparisons as descriptive rather than formally independent tests.

### Table 9d: Domain Overlap by Cell Type

```{r goal5-ct-domain}
# ── Data provenance ──
# ct_membership: named list from prot_v2, key = "ref_id|comp_id", value = CT labels
#   (lowercase: "at", "dd", "do", "fb", "mv")
# pe$pair_key, dom$pair_key: pair-level keys matching ct_membership names
# Subsetting pe and dom by ct_membership to compute per-CT metrics

ct_domain_rows <- lapply(main_cts, function(ct) {
  ct_lower <- ct_map[ct]
  ct_keys <- names(ct_membership)[sapply(ct_membership, function(x) ct_lower %in% x)]

  pe_ct <- pe[pe$pair_key %in% ct_keys, ]
  dom_ct <- dom[dom$pair_key %in% ct_keys, ]

  n_pairs_ct <- length(ct_keys)
  n_cds_ct <- length(unique(pe_ct$pair_key))
  n_dom_ct <- length(unique(dom_ct$pair_key))
  n_dis_ct <- length(unique(dom_ct$pair_key[dom_ct$effect == "disrupted_lost"]))
  n_gai_ct <- length(unique(dom_ct$pair_key[dom_ct$effect == "gained_intact"]))

  data.frame(
    cell_type = ct,
    n_pairs = n_pairs_ct,
    n_cds_events = n_cds_ct,
    n_domain_overlap = n_dom_ct,
    pct_domain_overlap = round(100 * n_dom_ct / max(n_cds_ct, 1), 1),
    n_disrupted = n_dis_ct,
    n_gained = n_gai_ct)
})
ct_domain_table <- do.call(rbind, ct_domain_rows)

render_dt(ct_domain_table,
  caption = "Table 9d: Domain Overlap Summary by Cell Type")
```

Columns: **cell_type**; **n_pairs** = coding isoform pairs in this CT;
**n_cds_events** = pairs with ≥1 CDS-overlapping splice event;
**n_domain_overlap** = pairs with ≥1 Pfam domain affected;
**pct_domain_overlap** = % of CDS-event pairs with domain overlap;
**n_disrupted** = pairs with ≥1 disrupted domain; **n_gained** = pairs with ≥1
gained domain.

### Figure 11b: Direction × Cell Type

```{r goal5-ct-direction, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Expand events to CT level via ct_membership, then compute domain overlap rate
# by CT × direction. CMH test for overall direction × domain overlap association
# stratified by cell type.

ct_dir_rows <- list()
for (ct in main_cts) {
  ct_lower <- ct_map[ct]
  ct_keys <- names(ct_membership)[sapply(ct_membership, function(x) ct_lower %in% x)]
  pe_ct <- pe[pe$pair_key %in% ct_keys, ]

  for (dir in c("GAIN", "LOSS")) {
    events_dir <- pe_ct[pe_ct$direction == dir, ]
    n_dir <- nrow(events_dir)
    n_dom_dir <- sum(events_dir$has_domain_overlap)
    ct_dir_rows[[length(ct_dir_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
      cell_type = ct, direction = dir,
      n_events = n_dir, n_dom = n_dom_dir,
      pct_dom = round(100 * n_dom_dir / max(n_dir, 1), 1))
  }
}
ct_dir_df <- do.call(rbind, ct_dir_rows)

fig11b <- ggplot(ct_dir_df, aes(x = cell_type, y = pct_dom, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", pct_dom)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(GAIN = "#4393c3", LOSS = "#d6604d")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(ct_dir_df$pct_dom) * 1.2),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  labs(title = "Domain Overlap Rate by Direction and Cell Type",
       subtitle = "% of CDS-overlapping events that overlap ≥1 Pfam domain",
       x = "Cell Type", y = "% Events with Domain Overlap", fill = "Direction") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

save_fig(fig11b, "fig11b_direction_by_celltype", width = 10, height = 5)

# CMH test: direction × domain overlap, stratified by CT
# Build 3D array: 2 (direction) × 2 (domain overlap) × 5 (CT)
cmh_array <- array(0L, dim = c(2, 2, length(main_cts)),
  dimnames = list(direction = c("GAIN", "LOSS"),
                  domain = c("overlap", "no_overlap"),
                  ct = main_cts))

for (i in seq_along(main_cts)) {
  ct <- main_cts[i]
  ct_lower <- ct_map[ct]
  ct_keys <- names(ct_membership)[sapply(ct_membership, function(x) ct_lower %in% x)]
  pe_ct <- pe[pe$pair_key %in% ct_keys, ]

  for (dir in c("GAIN", "LOSS")) {
    events_dir <- pe_ct[pe_ct$direction == dir, ]
    cmh_array[dir, "overlap", i] <- sum(events_dir$has_domain_overlap)
    cmh_array[dir, "no_overlap", i] <- sum(!events_dir$has_domain_overlap)
  }
}

cmh_test <- mantelhaen.test(cmh_array)
```

GAIN events consistently show higher domain overlap rates than LOSS events
across all cell types (Figure 11b). A Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test confirms
this association is significant when stratified by cell type (common OR =
`r round(cmh_test$estimate, 2)`, p = `r signif(cmh_test$p.value, 3)`).

**Note:** Because pairs can appear in multiple cell types, CT strata are not
fully independent. The CMH test assumes independent strata; the p-value should
be interpreted conservatively.

### Table 9e: Cell-Type-Specific Domain Enrichment

```{r goal5-ct-domain-enrichment, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# ── Data provenance ──
# For each Pfam domain: build a 2×5 table (affected/not × 5 CTs).
# Denominator per CT: pairs with CDS events in that CT.
# Test: chi-squared with Monte Carlo simulation (handles sparse cells).
# H0: the rate at which domain X is affected is the same across all CTs.
# BH correction across tested domains.

# Pre-compute per-CT CDS-event pair sets and domain-affected pair sets
ct_cds_keys <- list()
ct_dom_affected <- list()  # pair_key → pfam_acc affected
for (ct in main_cts) {
  ct_lower <- ct_map[ct]
  ct_keys <- names(ct_membership)[sapply(ct_membership, function(x) ct_lower %in% x)]
  ct_cds_keys[[ct]] <- unique(pe$pair_key[pe$pair_key %in% ct_keys])
  dom_ct <- dom[dom$pair_key %in% ct_keys, ]
  ct_dom_affected[[ct]] <- dom_ct[, c("pair_key", "pfam_acc")]
}

# Get all domains with ≥10 total affected pairs across CTs AND ≥2 CTs with ≥1
all_doms <- unique(dom$pfam_acc)
dom_ct_counts <- list()
for (d in all_doms) {
  cts_with <- 0L
  total <- 0L
  per_ct <- integer(length(main_cts))
  names(per_ct) <- main_cts
  for (j in seq_along(main_cts)) {
    ct <- main_cts[j]
    n_aff <- length(unique(ct_dom_affected[[ct]]$pair_key[
      ct_dom_affected[[ct]]$pfam_acc == d]))
    per_ct[j] <- n_aff
    total <- total + n_aff
    if (n_aff > 0) cts_with <- cts_with + 1L
  }
  if (total >= 10 && cts_with >= 2) {
    dom_ct_counts[[d]] <- per_ct
  }
}

n_ct_enrich_tested <- length(dom_ct_counts)

# Run chi-squared tests
ct_enrich_results <- list()
set.seed(42)  # reproducibility for Monte Carlo
for (d in names(dom_ct_counts)) {
  affected <- dom_ct_counts[[d]]
  n_cds <- sapply(main_cts, function(ct) length(ct_cds_keys[[ct]]))
  not_affected <- n_cds - affected

  # 2×5 matrix: rows = affected/not, cols = CTs
  mat <- rbind(affected, not_affected)

  # Monte Carlo for p-value (handles sparse cells)
  ct_mc <- tryCatch(
    chisq.test(mat, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 10000),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  # Standard chi-squared for residuals (stdres not available with simulation)
  ct_std <- tryCatch(
    chisq.test(mat),
    error = function(e) NULL)

  if (!is.null(ct_mc) && !is.null(ct_std)) {
    std_res <- ct_std$stdres[1, ]
    ct_enrich_results[[d]] <- data.frame(
      pfam_acc = d,
      chisq = round(ct_mc$statistic, 2),
      p_value = ct_mc$p.value,
      max_residual_ct = names(which.max(std_res)),
      max_residual = round(max(std_res), 2),
      min_residual_ct = names(which.min(std_res)),
      min_residual = round(min(std_res), 2),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
}

ct_enrich_df <- do.call(rbind, ct_enrich_results)
ct_enrich_df$padj <- p.adjust(ct_enrich_df$p_value, method = "BH")
ct_enrich_df$significant <- ct_enrich_df$padj < 0.05
ct_enrich_df <- ct_enrich_df[order(ct_enrich_df$p_value), ]

# Add domain name lookup
dom_name_lk <- setNames(dom$domain_name, dom$pfam_acc)
dom_name_lk <- dom_name_lk[!duplicated(names(dom_name_lk))]
ct_enrich_df$domain_name <- dom_name_lk[ct_enrich_df$pfam_acc]

n_ct_enrich_sig <- sum(ct_enrich_df$significant, na.rm = TRUE)

# Add per-CT percentage columns to ALL tested domains (needed for display)
for (ct in main_cts) {
  ct_enrich_df[[paste0("pct_", ct)]] <- sapply(ct_enrich_df$pfam_acc, function(d) {
    n_aff <- dom_ct_counts[[d]][ct]
    n_cds <- length(ct_cds_keys[[ct]])
    round(100 * n_aff / max(n_cds, 1), 2)
  })
}

ct_enrich_sig <- ct_enrich_df[ct_enrich_df$significant == TRUE &
                                !is.na(ct_enrich_df$significant), ]

display_cols <- c("pfam_acc", "domain_name",
  paste0("pct_", main_cts), "chisq", "padj",
  "max_residual_ct", "max_residual", "min_residual_ct", "min_residual")

if (nrow(ct_enrich_sig) > 0) {
  ct_enrich_display <- head(ct_enrich_sig[, display_cols], 30)
  ct_enrich_display$padj <- signif(ct_enrich_display$padj, 3)
  render_dt(ct_enrich_display,
    caption = sprintf("Table 9e: Domains with Cell-Type-Specific Enrichment (FDR < 0.05, %s tested)",
                      fmt(n_ct_enrich_tested)))
} else {
  cat("No domains with significant cell-type heterogeneity at FDR < 0.05.\n")
}
```

Of `r fmt(n_ct_enrich_tested)` Pfam domains tested (≥10 affected pairs across
≥2 cell types), **`r fmt(n_ct_enrich_sig)`** show significant heterogeneity in
their rate of being affected across cell types (chi-squared with Monte Carlo
simulation, BH-adjusted p < 0.05).

Columns: **pfam_acc** = Pfam accession; **domain_name**; **pct_AT** through
**pct_MV** = % of CDS-event pairs in each CT where this domain is affected;
**chisq** = chi-squared statistic; **padj** = BH-adjusted p-value;
**max_residual_ct** = cell type with the largest positive standardized residual
(most enriched); **max_residual** = that residual value; **min_residual_ct** =
cell type with the largest negative residual (most depleted);
**min_residual** = that residual value.

### Figure 11c: Cell-Type-Specific Domain Heatmap

```{r goal5-ct-domain-heatmap, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Standardized residuals from the chi-squared tests above.
# Positive residual = domain affected more than expected in that CT.
# Negative residual = affected less than expected.

if (nrow(ct_enrich_sig) > 0) {
  # Build residual matrix for top significant domains (up to 30)
  top_doms <- head(ct_enrich_sig$pfam_acc, 30)

  resid_rows <- list()
  for (d in top_doms) {
    affected <- dom_ct_counts[[d]]
    n_cds <- sapply(main_cts, function(ct) length(ct_cds_keys[[ct]]))
    not_affected <- n_cds - affected
    mat <- rbind(affected, not_affected)
    ct_test <- chisq.test(mat)  # standard chi-sq for stdres
    resid_rows[[d]] <- ct_test$stdres[1, ]
  }

  resid_mat <- do.call(rbind, resid_rows)
  rownames(resid_mat) <- paste0(dom_name_lk[top_doms], " (", top_doms, ")")

  # Reshape for ggplot
  resid_df <- data.frame(
    domain = rep(rownames(resid_mat), ncol(resid_mat)),
    cell_type = rep(colnames(resid_mat), each = nrow(resid_mat)),
    residual = as.vector(resid_mat),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  resid_df$domain <- factor(resid_df$domain, levels = rev(rownames(resid_mat)))

  # Cap residuals at ±4 for color scale
  resid_df$residual_capped <- pmin(pmax(resid_df$residual, -4), 4)

  fig11c <- ggplot(resid_df, aes(x = cell_type, y = domain, fill = residual_capped)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(residual, 1)), size = 3) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b",
                         midpoint = 0, limits = c(-4, 4),
                         name = "Std. Residual") +
    labs(title = "Cell-Type-Specific Domain Enrichment",
         subtitle = sprintf("Top %d domains with significant heterogeneity (FDR < 0.05). Positive = enriched, negative = depleted.",
                            length(top_doms)),
         x = "Cell Type", y = "") +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
          panel.grid = element_blank())

  save_fig(fig11c, "fig11c_ct_domain_heatmap", width = 10, height = max(4, length(top_doms) * 0.35))
} else {
  cat("No domains with significant cell-type heterogeneity at FDR < 0.05.\n")
}
```

The heatmap displays standardized residuals from the chi-squared tests. A
positive residual (red) indicates the domain is affected more frequently than
expected in that cell type; a negative residual (blue) indicates less frequently.
Residuals beyond ±2 are conventionally considered noteworthy.

**Non-independence caveat:** Pairs shared across cell types contribute to
multiple columns. This inflates chi-squared statistics and may produce
anti-conservative p-values. The results identify candidate CT-specific domain
patterns, but formal confirmation would require CT-exclusive pair analysis or a
mixed-effects framework.

# 6. Cross-Cell-Type Summary {#summary}

```{r sec6-summary-table}
# ── Data provenance ──
# Starting data: gene-matched profiles and cached analyses across all cell types
# Each row computed via helper functions that access set_results[[key]]:
#   - Pair counts: nrow(gene-matched profiles)
#   - PTC rates: compute_ptc_rates_row() — coding pairs from gene-matched profiles + ptc.rds
#   - Divergence: compute_divergence_row() — from cached quantifyPairDivergence()
#   - Productive frameshifts: from pf_data precompute (all_samples only)
# All helpers operate on gene-matched data (profiles_list was matched in STAGE 2)

summary_rows <- lapply(c("all_samples", main_cts), function(ct) {
  ct_label <- ct_to_label(ct)

  # NMD and Control pair counts
  c2_key <- paste0("c2_", ct_label)
  c4_key <- paste0("c4_", ct_label)
  n_nmd  <- if (c2_key %in% names(set_results)) nrow(set_results[[c2_key]]$profiles) else NA
  n_ctrl <- if (c4_key %in% names(set_results)) nrow(set_results[[c4_key]]$profiles) else NA

  # PTC rates
  ptc_row <- compute_ptc_rates_row(ct)
  ptc_rate_nmd  <- if (!is.null(ptc_row)) ptc_row$NMD_comp_ptc_pct else NA
  ptc_rate_ctrl <- if (!is.null(ptc_row)) ptc_row$Ctrl_comp_ptc_pct else NA
  ptc_or        <- if (!is.null(ptc_row)) ptc_row$fisher_OR else NA

  # PTC-neg %
  ptc_neg_pct <- if (!is.null(ptc_row)) round(100 - ptc_row$NMD_comp_ptc_pct, 1) else NA

  # Median pct_shared for C4
  div_row <- compute_divergence_row(ct)
  med_shared <- if (!is.null(div_row)) div_row$Ctrl_median_pct_shared else NA

  # Productive frameshifts (only available for all_samples)
  n_pf <- if (ct == "all_samples") nrow(pf_data$characterization) else NA

  data.frame(
    cell_type = ct,
    N_NMD_pairs = n_nmd,
    N_Ctrl_pairs = n_ctrl,
    PTC_rate_NMD_pct = ptc_rate_nmd,
    PTC_rate_Ctrl_pct = ptc_rate_ctrl,
    PTC_OR = ptc_or,
    PTC_neg_pct = ptc_neg_pct,
    Median_pct_shared_C4 = med_shared,
    N_productive_FS = n_pf)
})

summary_table <- do.call(rbind, summary_rows)
render_dt(summary_table, caption = "Table 11: Cross-Cell-Type Summary")
write.csv(summary_table, file.path(table_dir, "table11_cross_ct_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

Columns: **cell_type** = sample set; **N_NMD/N_Ctrl_pairs** = gene-matched pair
counts; **PTC_rate_NMD/Ctrl_pct** = PTC rate among coding comparators;
**PTC_OR** = Fisher OR for PTC enrichment; **PTC_neg_pct** = percentage of
coding NMD comparators without PTC; **Median_pct_shared_C4** = median exonic
sequence shared in Control pairs (from `quantifyPairDivergence()`);
**N_productive_FS** = productive frameshifts (all_samples only).
